Financial Highlights
Consolidated revenue at ₹50,105 Cr. up 26% YoY driven by all-round performance across its diversified businesses portfolio 
›
Standalone revenue stood all-time high of ₹12,747 Cr., up 33% YoY, led by double engine momentum from both Core and Growth businesses
›
Consolidated EBITDA up by 25% YoY to ₹6,513 Cr., mainly led by Cellulosic Staple Fibres, Building Materials and Financial Services businesses
Financial 
Performance
Revenue up by 15% YoY to ₹2,759 Cr. led by all-round performance across Caustic, Chlorine Derivatives and Specialty Chemicals
›
EBITDA down by 11% YoY due to higher power costs in Caustic and lower profitability in Specialty Chemicals business
›
Specialty Chemicals profitability impacted due to elevated input prices and softer demand across end-user industries
Chemicals
Revenue stood at ₹23,295 Cr., up 19% YoY mainly led by volume growth of 12.9% YoY to 38.2 million tons
›
Grey cement capacity up by 4.6 mtpa, taking total capacity (India and Overseas) to 210.1 mtpa; aim to achieve 242.9 mtpa by exit of Mar-28
›
EBITDA up by 17% YoY to ₹3,832 Cr. (₹974/ton) driven by revenue growth and lower power cost
Cement
Revenue stood at ₹1,337 Cr. up by 35% YoY (up 50% YoY for H1FY27), outpacing organised decorative paints industry growth
›
Expect to cross double-digit Revenue Market Share (RMS) in H2FY27 based on Oct-26 run-rate and rising brand confidence from consumers, influencers & retailers
›
Seasonally weak quarter impacted by input-cost inflation due to ongoing middle east crisis, rupee deprecation and competitive intensity
Paints
Revenue (Ind-AS) stood at ₹13,990 Cr., up 32% YoY led by broad-based growth across lending, insurance and asset management
›
Total Lending portfolio (NBFC and HFC) up by 32% YoY to ₹2,33,930 Cr.; Assets Under Management (AMC, life and health insurance) stood at ₹12,33,906 Cr. 
›
D2C platform - ABCD, witnessed strong response with more than 13.2 million customer acquisitions^
Financial 
Services
Revenue grew by 29% YoY to ₹5,344 Cr., led by volume growth, favorable product mix and stability in domestic prices
›
Segment EBITDA stood at ₹522 Cr., supported by revenue growth, partially offset by higher input costs mainly sulphur, power and pulp
›
CFY business performance remains muted amid subdued downstream demand, elevated sulphur cost and continued low-priced imports from China
Cellulosic 
Fibres
Revenue at ₹2,785 Cr. up by 66% YoY led by growth across large categories - Building materials, Metals and Chemicals 
›
Gross margins continue to improve; EBITDA impacted by one-time employee-related expenses; on track to achieve break-even in H2FY27
›
Large product categories driving scale, while private label categories Tiles, Plywood and Bathware are driving premiumisation

Press Release (13th November 2026): Grasim Industries Limited (BSE: 500300, NSE: GRASIM) today announced 
its financial results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.  
Key Highlights (Standalone) 
• 
Revenue stood highest-ever at ₹12,747 Cr., up 33% YoY;  
• 
EBITDA stood at ₹4,615 Cr., up 158% YoY; 
•

• 
Reported PAT stood at ₹2,306 Cr., up 187% YoY, accounting for exceptional charge of ₹825 Cr. towards 
impairment/estimated exposure in pulp JV, AV Group NB Inc., Canada. 
        STANDALONE FINANCIAL RESULTS                                                        ₹ Cr.

as compared to Consolidated results. The dividend from UltraTech of ₹3,968 Cr. is cash received by the 
Company, which is accounted in Standalone results, however, gets eliminated in Consolidated results.” 
Key Highlights (Consolidated) 
•

• 
EBITDA stood at ₹6,513 Cr., up 25% YoY; 
• 
Adjusted PAT (before exceptional items) stood at ₹536 Cr.; 
• 
Reported PAT stood at loss of ₹234 Cr. accounting for exceptional charge of ₹767 Cr. towards 
impairment/estimated exposure in pulp JV, AV Group NB Inc., Canada. 
                    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL RESULTS                                                       ₹ Cr.

Key Business Highlights 
✓ 
Cellulosic Fibres: Revenue up 29% YoY led by volume growth & favorable product mix 
✓ 
Chemicals: Revenue up 15% YoY led by Chlorine derivatives & resilience in Caustic-soda 
✓ 
Cement: Revenue up 19% YoY, mainly led by volume growth and pricing discipline 
✓ 
Birla Opus: Revenue at ₹1,337 Cr., up by 35% YoY, aim to cross double-digit RMS* in H2FY27 
✓ 
Birla Pivot: Revenue at ₹2,785 Cr., up by 66% YoY, ARR trending above ₹11,000 Cr. 
✓ 
Financial Services: Total Lending portfolio (NBFC + HFC) grew 32% YoY to ₹2,33,930 Cr. 

 
 
2 
 
Standalone: Revenue for Q2FY27 reached an all-time high of ₹12,747 Cr., up 33% YoY, led by continued 
growth momentum across Core and Growth businesses. Despite global volatility, key businesses, Cellulosic 
Fibres, Chemicals and Textiles continues to demonstrate resilience. Growth engines, Paints and B2B E-
commerce businesses continue their momentum, with strong consumer and brand traction. EBITDA stood 
at ₹4,615 Cr., up by 158% YoY, led by dividend income from UltraTech of ₹3,968 Cr. & favourable product 
mix, partially offset by higher inputs prices. Cash profit for Q2FY27 stood at ₹3,968 Cr., up 151% YoY.  
Consolidated: On a trailing twelve-month basis, consolidated revenues stood at ₹1,94,234 Cr., up by 11% 
vs. FY26, now at a striking distance of ₹2,00,000 Cr. The TTM EBITDA stood at ₹28,816 Cr., up 11% vs. FY26 
mainly led by Cellulosic Staple Fibres, Building Materials and Financial Services businesses. The Standalone 
business now contributes nearly 24% to the Consolidated Revenue and EBITDA.  The TTM PAT (owners share) 
before exceptional items stood at ₹5,861 Cr., up 13% vs. FY26. 
Cellulosic Fibres (Cellulosic Staple Fibres: CSF and Cellulosic Fashion Yarn: CFY) 
China’s CSF market remained strong, with operating rates at 93% in Q2FY27 vs. 89% in Q2FY26. Inventories 
continue to remain low at 6 days at the end of Q2FY27, signaling a healthy demand-supply balance. Global 
CSF prices have now risen for four consecutive quarters, with the Q2FY27 average at $1.85/kg, up 23% YoY. 
Higher global prices, coupled with rupee depreciation, have led to stability in domestic realisation.  
Grasim’s CSF sales volumes stood at 224 KT, up 7% YoY, mainly driven by strong exports. CFY volumes grew 
by 2% YoY to 11.6 KT, amid subdued downstream demand from end-user industries, however, EBITDA was 
lower due to elevated sulphur cost and continued low-priced imports from China. Cellulosic Fibres segment 
revenue grew by 29% YoY to ₹5,344 Cr., supported by volume growth, favourable product mix and stable 
domestic realisation, despite geo-political issues and higher input and logistics costs. EBITDA stood at ₹522 
Cr., up 49% YoY, aided by revenue growth and higher share of specialty fibres. 
Chemicals (Caustic-soda, Chlorine Derivatives and Specialty Chemicals) 
Caustic soda international average spot prices (CFR-SEA) stood at five-year low levels of $390/ton in 
Q2FY27, down by 13% YoY. Despite softness in global caustic soda prices, domestic realisations remain 
relatively resilient, supported by rupee depreciation, healthy end-user demand, lower import dependence 
and tighter domestic supply pan-India availability. Chemicals business, caustic sales volumes stood at 317 
KT, up 8% YoY. Chlorine realisation continues to remain negative, which resulted in moderation of ECU which 
was marginally up by 2% YoY to ₹33,587/ton.  
Chemicals segment revenue stood at ₹2,759 Cr., up 15% YoY led to volume growth and robust performance 
in Chlorine derivatives business. Specialty Chemicals revenue share, in the overall Chemicals segment, 
stood at 28%. EBITDA stood at ₹326 Cr., down by 11% YoY due to higher power costs in Caustic and lower 
profitability in Specialty Chemicals business. Specialty Chemicals profitability impacted due to elevated 
input prices and softer demand across end-user industries. 
Building Materials (Cement, Paints and B2B E-commerce) 
Building Materials revenue stood at ₹27,378 Cr., up 23% YoY, led by all-round performance across Cement, 
Paints and B2B E-commerce. EBITDA stood at ₹3,510 Cr., up 19% YoY, led by improved profitability in the 
Cement business. This was partially offset by higher investments in Paints business to address input-cost 
inflation, rupee deprecation and competitive intensity and one-time employee-related expenses in B2B E-
commerce business.  
Cement business, UltraTech’s consolidated sales volumes stood at 38.2 MT, up by 12.9% YoY and ready-mix 
concrete sales volumes grew by 23% YoY to 4.7 Mn m3. During the quarter, UltraTech added 4.6 mtpa of 

 
 
3 
 
grey cement capacity, taking total capacity (India + Overseas) to 210.1 mtpa. The business has target to 
reach total grey cement capacity of 242.9 mtpa by exit of FY28. UltraTech Building Solutions (UBS) outlets 
increased to 6,289, up by 1,205 outlets on YoY basis. Green power mix for Q2Y27 stood at 46.4% with a target 
to reach 85% by FY30. Cement business revenue stood at ₹23,295 Cr., up 19% YoY mainly led by volume 
growth. 
Decorative Paints business, Birla Opus, is shifting focus from rapid market entry towards building a stronger, 
sustainable and profitable market share. Traditionally, Q2FY27 remains a weak quarter due to monsoon-
related slowdown in decorative paints and higher competitive intensity. Despite challenging market 
conditions, the combined market share, including Birla White Putty, remained in the early teens. The 
revenue for Q2FY27 stood at ₹1,337 Cr., up 35% YoY and for H1FY27 stood at ₹2,999 Cr., up 50% YoY, 
outpacing organised decorative paints industry growth.  
The Q2 volume grew by 20% YoY & H1FY27 volume grew by 33% YoY. The focus extends beyond quarterly 
seasonality towards building a business capable of converting market acceleration into enduring growth. 
Distribution network expanded to +61,000 first-time billed dealers across 12,600+ towns, with 1,760+ franchise 
stores, ~150 depots, and nearly 10,000 institutional project sites billed during Q2. Its expanding distribution, 
exclusive franchisee footprint, brand investment, product portfolio quality, and customer & influencer 
engagement are creating momentum for H2FY27. ‘Birla Opus’ aims to cross double-digit revenue market 
share of Indian Organised Decorative Paints market, in H2FY27. The portfolio reached 239 products, while 
aided brand awareness scores reached enviable 92%; giving confidence to deliver guided revenue of 
₹10,000 Cr. by exit of FY28. 
B2B E-Commerce business, Birla Pivot growth momentum continues, reflecting a stronger value proposition 
across price, assortment and experience. The revenue stood at ₹2,785 Cr., up 66% YoY with annualized 
revenue run-rate (ARR) now above ₹11,000 Cr; one of the fastest growing companies in India’s B2B E-
commerce landscape. Project and retail business account for 90% and 10% of revenue respectively. The 
product portfolio continues to diversify. Building Materials, Non-Ferrous Metals and Chemicals are the key 
growth drivers, and assortment is deepening in high-potential categories. Private labels are gaining traction 
across Birla Pivot Ply, Tiles and Bathware. Gross margins continue to improve gradually however Q2FY27 
EBITDA was affected by one-time employee expenses. The business aims to cross ₹120 billion in revenue for 
FY27 and remains on track to EBITDA profitability in H2FY27, focusing on category economics & cost control.  
Financial Services 
Aditya Birla Capital continued its strong growth trajectory in Q2FY27, delivering consolidated revenue, in 
accordance with Ind-AS, of ₹13,990 Cr., registering a growth of 32% YoY. The performance reflects sustained 
growth momentum across its diversified financial services businesses, supported by disciplined execution, 
improving profitability and a focus on quality growth. The total lending portfolio (NBFC + HFC) stood at 
₹2,33,930 Cr., up 32% YoY, while customer assets across its asset management and insurance businesses 
stood at ₹12,33,906 Cr., reflecting the strength of its integrated financial services franchise. The company 
continues to accelerate its digital and technology transformation, with AI-led initiatives being deployed 
across underwriting, customer engagement, operations and claims management to enhance productivity 
and customer experience.  
 
Other Businesses (Textiles, Renewables, and Insulators) 

 
 
4 
 
Other businesses reported revenue of ₹1,158 Cr., up 16% YoY, while EBITDA stood at ₹284 Cr., up14% YoY. 
Textiles revenue grew by 24% YoY to ₹729 Cr., and its EBITDA more than doubled YoY to ₹55 Cr. from ₹24 Cr. 
in Q2FY26 due to improved performance of linen business. Renewables revenue for Q2FY27 stood at ₹250 
Cr., and EBITDA stood at ₹205 Cr. The business has higher base due to one-time revenue of ₹54 Cr. on 
account of rate differential. Cumulative installed peak capacity stood at 2.2 GW, up 269 MWp YoY, with 
49% of capacity serving Group companies. Insulator business revenue stood at ₹158 Cr., up 17% YoY and 
EBITDA stood at ₹20 Cr., up 35% YoY. 
Capital Expenditure 
The FY27 capex budget is ₹3,157 Cr. across all Grasim Standalone businesses, with nearly 45% allocated to 
growth projects. The total capex spent for H1FY27 stood at ₹1,022 Cr. Lyocell capacity expansion project, 
Phase I (55K TPA), procurement delivery is nearing completion, with cumulative capex spent at ₹420 Cr. For 
Phase II (110K TPA) Lyocell expansion project, the Environmental Clearance application is at an advanced 
stage of submission.  
Sustainability 
The Company is advancing its environmental goals by expanding clean energy use and improving water 
circularity across its manufacturing sites. On a standalone basis, the share of renewable capacity power in 
total power requirement rose to 26% in H1FY27 (vs. 24% in FY26), while recycled and reused water to 
freshwater withdrawal stood at 51% in H1FY27. 
Outlook 
As India advances towards its vision of Viksit Bharat, sustained investments in infrastructure, manufacturing, 
housing and the energy transition are expected to create significant growth opportunities across Grasim's 
businesses. With its strong foundation in Cellulosic Fibres and Chemicals, alongside the scaling up of its 
growth engines in Paints, B2B E-commerce and Renewables, Grasim is well positioned to participate in 
India's expanding consumption and infrastructure opportunity. The Company's disciplined capital 
allocation, ongoing investments in capacity expansion, focus on operational efficiencies and commitment 
to sustainability provide a strong foundation for its next phase of growth. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
About Grasim Industries Limited 
Grasim Industries Limited, a flagship company of the Aditya Birla Group, ranks amongst the top publicly listed companies in India. Incorporated in 1947, it started as a textiles manufacturer in India. Today, it has evolved into a leading diversified player with 
leadership presence across many sectors. It is a leading global producer of Cellulosic Fibres and one of the largest producers of Diversified Chemicals, Fashion Yarn and Fabrics producer in India. Implementing next phase of transformational growth 
journey, the company has entered paints business under the brand name ‘Birla Opus’. All six state-of-the-art greenfield plants have commenced commercial production, and our total installed capacity is 1,332 million litres per annum (MLPA). Leveraging 
the Group synergies, Grasim has launched ‘Birla Pivot’, the B2B online marketplace for building materials. Through its subsidiaries, UltraTech Cement, Aditya Birla Capital and Aditya Birla Renewables, it is also India’s prominent cement producer, leading 
diversified financial services player and clean energy solutions player. At Grasim, there is an endeavour to create sustainable value for 45,000+ employees, 2,52,000+ shareholders, society, and customers.

Press Release (13th November 2026): Grasim Industries Limited (BSE: 500300, NSE: GRASIM) today announced 
its financial results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.

Key Business Highlights 
✓ 
Cellulosic Fibres: Revenue up 29% YoY led by volume growth & favorable product mix 
✓ 
Chemicals: Revenue up 15% YoY led by Chlorine derivatives & resilience in Caustic-soda 
✓ 
Cement: Revenue up 19% YoY, mainly led by volume growth and pricing discipline 
✓ 
Birla Opus: Revenue at ₹1,337 Cr., up by 35% YoY, aim to cross double-digit RMS* in H2FY27 
✓ 
Birla Pivot: Revenue at ₹2,785 Cr., up by 66% YoY, ARR trending above ₹11,000 Cr. 
✓ 
Financial Services: Total Lending portfolio (NBFC + HFC) grew 32% YoY to ₹2,33,930 Cr. 

 
 
2 
 
Standalone: Revenue for Q2FY27 reached an all-time high of ₹12,747 Cr., up 33% YoY, led by continued 
growth momentum across Core and Growth businesses. Despite global volatility, key businesses, Cellulosic 
Fibres, Chemicals and Textiles continues to demonstrate resilience. Growth engines, Paints and B2B E-
commerce businesses continue their momentum, with strong consumer and brand traction. EBITDA stood 
at ₹4,615 Cr., up by 158% YoY, led by dividend income from UltraTech of ₹3,968 Cr. & favourable product 
mix, partially offset by higher inputs prices. Cash profit for Q2FY27 stood at ₹3,968 Cr., up 151% YoY.  
Consolidated: On a trailing twelve-month basis, consolidated revenues stood at ₹1,94,234 Cr., up by 11% 
vs. FY26, now at a striking distance of ₹2,00,000 Cr. The TTM EBITDA stood at ₹28,816 Cr., up 11% vs. FY26 
mainly led by Cellulosic Staple Fibres, Building Materials and Financial Services businesses. The Standalone 
business now contributes nearly 24% to the Consolidated Revenue and EBITDA.  The TTM PAT (owners share) 
before exceptional items stood at ₹5,861 Cr., up 13% vs. FY26. 
Cellulosic Fibres (Cellulosic Staple Fibres: CSF and Cellulosic Fashion Yarn: CFY) 
China’s CSF market remained strong, with operating rates at 93% in Q2FY27 vs. 89% in Q2FY26. Inventories 
continue to remain low at 6 days at the end of Q2FY27, signaling a healthy demand-supply balance. Global 
CSF prices have now risen for four consecutive quarters, with the Q2FY27 average at $1.85/kg, up 23% YoY. 
Higher global prices, coupled with rupee depreciation, have led to stability in domestic realisation.  
Grasim’s CSF sales volumes stood at 224 KT, up 7% YoY, mainly driven by strong exports. CFY volumes grew 
by 2% YoY to 11.6 KT, amid subdued downstream demand from end-user industries, however, EBITDA was 
lower due to elevated sulphur cost and continued low-priced imports from China. Cellulosic Fibres segment 
revenue grew by 29% YoY to ₹5,344 Cr., supported by volume growth, favourable product mix and stable 
domestic realisation, despite geo-political issues and higher input and logistics costs. EBITDA stood at ₹522 
Cr., up 49% YoY, aided by revenue growth and higher share of specialty fibres. 
Chemicals (Caustic-soda, Chlorine Derivatives and Specialty Chemicals) 
Caustic soda international average spot prices (CFR-SEA) stood at five-year low levels of $390/ton in 
Q2FY27, down by 13% YoY. Despite softness in global caustic soda prices, domestic realisations remain 
relatively resilient, supported by rupee depreciation, healthy end-user demand, lower import dependence 
and tighter domestic supply pan-India availability. Chemicals business, caustic sales volumes stood at 317 
KT, up 8% YoY. Chlorine realisation continues to remain negative, which resulted in moderation of ECU which 
was marginally up by 2% YoY to ₹33,587/ton.  
Chemicals segment revenue stood at ₹2,759 Cr., up 15% YoY led to volume growth and robust performance 
in Chlorine derivatives business. Specialty Chemicals revenue share, in the overall Chemicals segment, 
stood at 28%. EBITDA stood at ₹326 Cr., down by 11% YoY due to higher power costs in Caustic and lower 
profitability in Specialty Chemicals business. Specialty Chemicals profitability impacted due to elevated 
input prices and softer demand across end-user industries. 
Building Materials (Cement, Paints and B2B E-commerce) 
Building Materials revenue stood at ₹27,378 Cr., up 23% YoY, led by all-round performance across Cement, 
Paints and B2B E-commerce. EBITDA stood at ₹3,510 Cr., up 19% YoY, led by improved profitability in the 
Cement business. This was partially offset by higher investments in Paints business to address input-cost 
inflation, rupee deprecation and competitive intensity and one-time employee-related expenses in B2B E-
commerce business.  
Cement business, UltraTech’s consolidated sales volumes stood at 38.2 MT, up by 12.9% YoY and ready-mix 
concrete sales volumes grew by 23% YoY to 4.7 Mn m3. During the quarter, UltraTech added 4.6 mtpa of 

 
 
3 
 
grey cement capacity, taking total capacity (India + Overseas) to 210.1 mtpa. The business has target to 
reach total grey cement capacity of 242.9 mtpa by exit of FY28. UltraTech Building Solutions (UBS) outlets 
increased to 6,289, up by 1,205 outlets on YoY basis. Green power mix for Q2Y27 stood at 46.4% with a target 
to reach 85% by FY30. Cement business revenue stood at ₹23,295 Cr., up 19% YoY mainly led by volume 
growth. 
Decorative Paints business, Birla Opus, is shifting focus from rapid market entry towards building a stronger, 
sustainable and profitable market share. Traditionally, Q2FY27 remains a weak quarter due to monsoon-
related slowdown in decorative paints and higher competitive intensity. Despite challenging market 
conditions, the combined market share, including Birla White Putty, remained in the early teens. The 
revenue for Q2FY27 stood at ₹1,337 Cr., up 35% YoY and for H1FY27 stood at ₹2,999 Cr., up 50% YoY, 
outpacing organised decorative paints industry growth.  
The Q2 volume grew by 20% YoY & H1FY27 volume grew by 33% YoY. The focus extends beyond quarterly 
seasonality towards building a business capable of converting market acceleration into enduring growth. 
Distribution network expanded to +61,000 first-time billed dealers across 12,600+ towns, with 1,760+ franchise 
stores, ~150 depots, and nearly 10,000 institutional project sites billed during Q2. Its expanding distribution, 
exclusive franchisee footprint, brand investment, product portfolio quality, and customer & influencer 
engagement are creating momentum for H2FY27. ‘Birla Opus’ aims to cross double-digit revenue market 
share of Indian Organised Decorative Paints market, in H2FY27. The portfolio reached 239 products, while 
aided brand awareness scores reached enviable 92%; giving confidence to deliver guided revenue of 
₹10,000 Cr. by exit of FY28. 
B2B E-Commerce business, Birla Pivot growth momentum continues, reflecting a stronger value proposition 
across price, assortment and experience. The revenue stood at ₹2,785 Cr., up 66% YoY with annualized 
revenue run-rate (ARR) now above ₹11,000 Cr; one of the fastest growing companies in India’s B2B E-
commerce landscape. Project and retail business account for 90% and 10% of revenue respectively. The 
product portfolio continues to diversify. Building Materials, Non-Ferrous Metals and Chemicals are the key 
growth drivers, and assortment is deepening in high-potential categories. Private labels are gaining traction 
across Birla Pivot Ply, Tiles and Bathware. Gross margins continue to improve gradually however Q2FY27 
EBITDA was affected by one-time employee expenses. The business aims to cross ₹120 billion in revenue for 
FY27 and remains on track to EBITDA profitability in H2FY27, focusing on category economics & cost control.  
Financial Services 
Aditya Birla Capital continued its strong growth trajectory in Q2FY27, delivering consolidated revenue, in 
accordance with Ind-AS, of ₹13,990 Cr., registering a growth of 32% YoY. The performance reflects sustained 
growth momentum across its diversified financial services businesses, supported by disciplined execution, 
improving profitability and a focus on quality growth. The total lending portfolio (NBFC + HFC) stood at 
₹2,33,930 Cr., up 32% YoY, while customer assets across its asset management and insurance businesses 
stood at ₹12,33,906 Cr., reflecting the strength of its integrated financial services franchise. The company 
continues to accelerate its digital and technology transformation, with AI-led initiatives being deployed 
across underwriting, customer engagement, operations and claims management to enhance productivity 
and customer experience.  
 
Other Businesses (Textiles, Renewables, and Insulators) 

 
 
4 
 
Other businesses reported revenue of ₹1,158 Cr., up 16% YoY, while EBITDA stood at ₹284 Cr., up14% YoY. 
Textiles revenue grew by 24% YoY to ₹729 Cr., and its EBITDA more than doubled YoY to ₹55 Cr. from ₹24 Cr. 
in Q2FY26 due to improved performance of linen business. Renewables revenue for Q2FY27 stood at ₹250 
Cr., and EBITDA stood at ₹205 Cr. The business has higher base due to one-time revenue of ₹54 Cr. on 
account of rate differential. Cumulative installed peak capacity stood at 2.2 GW, up 269 MWp YoY, with 
49% of capacity serving Group companies. Insulator business revenue stood at ₹158 Cr., up 17% YoY and 
EBITDA stood at ₹20 Cr., up 35% YoY. 
Capital Expenditure 
The FY27 capex budget is ₹3,157 Cr. across all Grasim Standalone businesses, with nearly 45% allocated to 
growth projects. The total capex spent for H1FY27 stood at ₹1,022 Cr. Lyocell capacity expansion project, 
Phase I (55K TPA), procurement delivery is nearing completion, with cumulative capex spent at ₹420 Cr. For 
Phase II (110K TPA) Lyocell expansion project, the Environmental Clearance application is at an advanced 
stage of submission.  
Sustainability 
The Company is advancing its environmental goals by expanding clean energy use and improving water 
circularity across its manufacturing sites. On a standalone basis, the share of renewable capacity power in 
total power requirement rose to 26% in H1FY27 (vs. 24% in FY26), while recycled and reused water to 
freshwater withdrawal stood at 51% in H1FY27. 
Outlook 
As India advances towards its vision of Viksit Bharat, sustained investments in infrastructure, manufacturing, 
housing and the energy transition are expected to create significant growth opportunities across Grasim's 
businesses. With its strong foundation in Cellulosic Fibres and Chemicals, alongside the scaling up of its 
growth engines in Paints, B2B E-commerce and Renewables, Grasim is well positioned to participate in 
India's expanding consumption and infrastructure opportunity. The Company's disciplined capital 
allocation, ongoing investments in capacity expansion, focus on operational efficiencies and commitment 
to sustainability provide a strong foundation for its next phase of growth. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
About Grasim Industries Limited 
Grasim Industries Limited, a flagship company of the Aditya Birla Group, ranks amongst the top publicly listed companies in India. Incorporated in 1947, it started as a textiles manufacturer in India. Today, it has evolved into a leading diversified player with 
leadership presence across many sectors. It is a leading global producer of Cellulosic Fibres and one of the largest producers of Diversified Chemicals, Fashion Yarn and Fabrics producer in India. Implementing next phase of transformational growth 
journey, the company has entered paints business under the brand name ‘Birla Opus’. All six state-of-the-art greenfield plants have commenced commercial production, and our total installed capacity is 1,332 million litres per annum (MLPA). Leveraging 
the Group synergies, Grasim has launched ‘Birla Pivot’, the B2B online marketplace for building materials. Through its subsidiaries, UltraTech Cement, Aditya Birla Capital and Aditya Birla Renewables, it is also India’s prominent cement producer, leading 
diversified financial services player and clean energy solutions player. At Grasim, there is an endeavour to create sustainable value for 45,000+ employees, 2,52,000+ shareholders, society, and customers.

The above financial results of the Company for the quarter and six months ended 30th September 2026 
have been reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors of the Company

Exceptional Items included in the results are as below: 
a) AV Group NB Inc ("AVNB"), a Joint Venture of the Company. has undertaken temporarily idling of 
operations of its dissolving grade pulp mill located Nackawic, New Brunswick, Canada, following a 
careful assessment of continuing challenges, prevailing market conditions and broader 
macroeconomic factors. Accordingly, during the quarter ended 30th September 2026, the Company 
has recognised an impairment charge of ₹187.42 crore against the carrying value of its investment in 
equity shares and preference shares of AVNB. Further, a provision has been created towards its 
estimated exposure of ₹638.0l crore. Total charge of ₹825.43 crore is recognised as an Exceptional 
Item. 
b) During the year ended 31st March 2026, the Company recognised charge of ₹47.86 crore as an 
Exceptional Item towards impairment of certain plant and equipment and building at the Chemical 
Vilayat facility, arising from persistent equipment failures and corrosion issues that ultimately led to 
the shutdown of the equipment. 
c) The Government of India has notified the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, 
the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health, and Working Conditions 
Code. 2020 (- Labour Codes- ) with effect from 21' November 2025, which consolidates 29 existing 
labour laws. The Labour Codes, amongst other things, introduced changes including a uniform 
definition of wages and enhanced benefits relating to leave. In accordance with the guidance issued 
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and based on actuarial valuation, the Company 
has assessed the impact of these regulatory changes towards additional Gratuity and Compensated 
absences and has recognised a charge of ₹34.17 crore, classified as past service cost disclosed under 
Exceptional Items in the financial results for the year ended 31' March 2026. 
d) Based on observable inputs, the Company had recognised a charge of ₹34 crore and ₹47.50 crore 
during the quarter and the year ended 31" March 2026, respectively, as Exceptional Items, towards 
estimated exposure in two of its Joint Venture entities (AV Terrace Bay Inc., Canada ₹34 crore and 
Birla Advanced Knits Private Limited ₹13.50 crore). 
Since the segment information as per Ind AS 108 — Operating Segments is provided in the consolidated 
financial results, the same is not provided in the standalone financial results.

TVS MOTOR EXPANDS BRAZIL OPERATIONS AND 
REINFORCES LONG-TERM COMMITMENT  
• 
New São Paulo Flagship Store anchors a broader strategy spanning local 
operational capacity, retail expansion and nationwide after-sales support. 
• With an annual production capacity of approximately 130,000 units, TVS is set to expand 
its retail network in partnership with Mottu, including three new stores during 2027. 
• This partnership provides access to ~500 points of sale, 168 service locations in Brazil. 
• The first TVS Motor Flagship Store opens at Avenida dos Bandeirantes, 1747, Vila 
Olímpia, São Paulo. 
 
Singapore, São Paulo, November 12, 2026: TVS Motor Company (TVSM), part of TVS VENU, the 
world's third-largest two-wheeler manufacturer, today announced the next phase of its growth in Brazil, 
supported by increased production capacity, an expanding retail footprint and a significant nationwide 
after-sales and service network. The opening of the company’s first Flagship Store in São Paulo 
provides a visible customer-facing proof point of this broader, long-term commitment to the Brazilian 
market. 
 
TVS Motor’s operations in Brazil currently have annual production capacity of approximately 
110,000 units in 2026, with plans to increase capacity to 130,000 units by 2027. The planned 
expansion is intended to support the company’s growing commercial presence and its long-term 
ambition to build a sustainable business in one of the world’s leading motorcycle markets.   
 
The growth plan also includes a wider retail and service presence. In partnership with Mottu, TVS 
Motor plans to renovate existing locations and open new exclusive dealerships, initially focusing on the 
Southeast and Central-West regions. Three new stores are planned during 2027, bringing the brand 
and its portfolio closer to customers.  
 
Through the partnership with Mottu, TVS Motor has access to a network of more than 500 points of 
sale and 168 service locations across Brazil. Locations authorised to service TVS models will have 
specialised technical teams trained by the manufacturer, supported by local spare-parts availability.  
 
Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor Company, said: "Brazil 
is a strategically important market for TVS Motor and a key pillar of our international growth 
ambitions. Through our partnership with Mottu, we are investing in our local capacity, 
expanding our retail footprint and strengthening the service ecosystem required to build a 
sustainable and enduring business for the years ahead. The opening of our first Flagship 
Store is an important milestone within this broader strategy, bringing TVS Motor closer to 
Brazilian consumers and enabling us to deliver innovative, high-quality products and 
experiences that resonate with local customers.”  
 
With a presence in more than 90 countries and over 50 million customers worldwide, TVS Motor has 
operated in 18 Latin American markets for more than 15 years. The expansion of its operations in Brazil 
is part of the company's international strategy, which identifies the Brazilian market as a significant 
opportunity to strengthen its regional operations and consolidate its presence in one of the world's 
leading motorcycle markets. 
First Flagship Store Strengthens Commercial Strategy 
The opening of the first Flagship Store represents a milestone in TVS Motor's brand positioning and 
commercial expansion strategy in Brazil. Featuring a 149 square metres showroom within a total area 
of approximately 250 square metres, the space was designed to bring the brand closer to Brazilian 
consumers by combining product displays, technology, and brand experience in a single environment. 

 
 
The new location also serves as a showcase for the manufacturer's portfolio and its approach to the 
Brazilian market, combining products developed for different consumer profiles with a local sales and 
customer service infrastructure. 
 
"The Brazilian two-wheeler market is one of the most dynamic and significant in the world, closely 
aligned with our global expertise in mobility. We want to offer Brazilian riders products that combine 
technology, design, and performance, supported by a strong customer service and after-sales 
infrastructure. The opening of our first Flagship Store in São Paulo represents an important milestone 
in bringing TVS closer to consumers and reaffirming our long-term commitment to the country," says 
Martin Corsunsky, Continental Business Head at TVS Motor Company. 
Partnership with Mottu Supports Expansion in the Brazilian Market 
TVS Motor's growth strategy in Brazil is supported by its partnership with Mottu, established four years 
ago. The collaboration combines the manufacturer's international expertise in motorcycle development 
with the Brazilian partner's local distribution, sales, and support infrastructure. 
 
Through this partnership, the brand's expansion plans includes the gradual opening of exclusive retail 
locations and strengthening the manufacturer's presence in priority markets.  
 
After-sales service is also a key component of this strategy. Locations authorized to service TVS models 
will have specialized technical teams trained by the manufacturer, as well as local spare parts 
availability. 
Portfolio Designed for Different Consumer Profiles 
The models presented include the TVS NTORQ 125, a sporty scooter featuring connectivity capabilities; 
the TVS Raider 125, designed for urban mobility with a focus on efficiency and technology; the TVS 
Apache 160, which combines performance and handling for everyday riding; and the TVS Apache 200, 
developed with racing-inspired technologies and a focus on the riding experience. 
 
The introduction of this portfolio is part of the manufacturer's strategy to consolidate its commercial 
presence in Brazil, expanding the mobility options available to consumers and reinforcing TVS Motor's 
positioning in the national market. 
 
About TVS Motor Company 
 
TVS Motor Company (BSE:532343 and NSE: TVSMOTOR), part of TVS VENU, is a reputed two and 
three-wheeler manufacturer globally, championing progress through sustainable mobility with four 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities located in India and Indonesia. Rooted in our 100-year legacy 
of trust, value, and passion for customers, it takes pride in making internationally accepted products of 
the highest quality through innovative and sustainable processes. TVS Motor is the only two-wheeler 
company to have won the prestigious Deming Prize. Our products lead in their respective categories in 
the J.D. Power IQS and APEAL surveys. We have been ranked No. 1 Company in the J.D. Power 
Customer Service Satisfaction Survey for four consecutive years. Our group company Norton 
Motorcycles, based in the United Kingdom, is one of the most emotive motorcycle brands in the world. 
TVS Motor Company endeavours to deliver the most superior customer experience across 90 countries 
in which we operate.  
 
For more information, please visit www.tvsmotor.com   
 
For further details, please contact: 
Kanika Mehta: kanika.mehta@tvsmotor.com

TVS MOTOR EXPANDS BRAZIL OPERATIONS AND 
REINFORCES LONG-TERM COMMITMENT  
• 
New São Paulo Flagship Store anchors a broader strategy spanning local 
operational capacity, retail expansion and nationwide after-sales support. 
• With an annual production capacity of approximately 130,000 units, TVS is set to expand 
its retail network in partnership with Mottu, including three new stores during 2027. 
• This partnership provides access to ~500 points of sale, 168 service locations in Brazil. 
• The first TVS Motor Flagship Store opens at Avenida dos Bandeirantes, 1747, Vila 
Olímpia, São Paulo. 
 
Singapore, São Paulo, November 12, 2026: TVS Motor Company (TVSM), part of TVS VENU, the 
world's third-largest two-wheeler manufacturer, today announced the next phase of its growth in Brazil, 
supported by increased production capacity, an expanding retail footprint and a significant nationwide 
after-sales and service network. The opening of the company’s first Flagship Store in São Paulo 
provides a visible customer-facing proof point of this broader, long-term commitment to the Brazilian 
market. 
 
TVS Motor’s operations in Brazil currently have annual production capacity of approximately 
110,000 units in 2026, with plans to increase capacity to 130,000 units by 2027. The planned 
expansion is intended to support the company’s growing commercial presence and its long-term 
ambition to build a sustainable business in one of the world’s leading motorcycle markets.   
 
The growth plan also includes a wider retail and service presence. In partnership with Mottu, TVS 
Motor plans to renovate existing locations and open new exclusive dealerships, initially focusing on the 
Southeast and Central-West regions. Three new stores are planned during 2027, bringing the brand 
and its portfolio closer to customers.  
 
Through the partnership with Mottu, TVS Motor has access to a network of more than 500 points of 
sale and 168 service locations across Brazil. Locations authorised to service TVS models will have 
specialised technical teams trained by the manufacturer, supported by local spare-parts availability.  
 
Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor Company, said: "Brazil 
is a strategically important market for TVS Motor and a key pillar of our international growth 
ambitions. Through our partnership with Mottu, we are investing in our local capacity, 
expanding our retail footprint and strengthening the service ecosystem required to build a 
sustainable and enduring business for the years ahead. The opening of our first Flagship 
Store is an important milestone within this broader strategy, bringing TVS Motor closer to 
Brazilian consumers and enabling us to deliver innovative, high-quality products and 
experiences that resonate with local customers.”  
 
With a presence in more than 90 countries and over 50 million customers worldwide, TVS Motor has 
operated in 18 Latin American markets for more than 15 years. The expansion of its operations in Brazil 
is part of the company's international strategy, which identifies the Brazilian market as a significant 
opportunity to strengthen its regional operations and consolidate its presence in one of the world's 
leading motorcycle markets. 
First Flagship Store Strengthens Commercial Strategy 
The opening of the first Flagship Store represents a milestone in TVS Motor's brand positioning and 
commercial expansion strategy in Brazil. Featuring a 149 square metres showroom within a total area 
of approximately 250 square metres, the space was designed to bring the brand closer to Brazilian 
consumers by combining product displays, technology, and brand experience in a single environment. 

 
 
The new location also serves as a showcase for the manufacturer's portfolio and its approach to the 
Brazilian market, combining products developed for different consumer profiles with a local sales and 
customer service infrastructure. 
 
"The Brazilian two-wheeler market is one of the most dynamic and significant in the world, closely 
aligned with our global expertise in mobility. We want to offer Brazilian riders products that combine 
technology, design, and performance, supported by a strong customer service and after-sales 
infrastructure. The opening of our first Flagship Store in São Paulo represents an important milestone 
in bringing TVS closer to consumers and reaffirming our long-term commitment to the country," says 
Martin Corsunsky, Continental Business Head at TVS Motor Company. 
Partnership with Mottu Supports Expansion in the Brazilian Market 
TVS Motor's growth strategy in Brazil is supported by its partnership with Mottu, established four years 
ago. The collaboration combines the manufacturer's international expertise in motorcycle development 
with the Brazilian partner's local distribution, sales, and support infrastructure. 
 
Through this partnership, the brand's expansion plans includes the gradual opening of exclusive retail 
locations and strengthening the manufacturer's presence in priority markets.  
 
After-sales service is also a key component of this strategy. Locations authorized to service TVS models 
will have specialized technical teams trained by the manufacturer, as well as local spare parts 
availability. 
Portfolio Designed for Different Consumer Profiles 
The models presented include the TVS NTORQ 125, a sporty scooter featuring connectivity capabilities; 
the TVS Raider 125, designed for urban mobility with a focus on efficiency and technology; the TVS 
Apache 160, which combines performance and handling for everyday riding; and the TVS Apache 200, 
developed with racing-inspired technologies and a focus on the riding experience. 
 
The introduction of this portfolio is part of the manufacturer's strategy to consolidate its commercial 
presence in Brazil, expanding the mobility options available to consumers and reinforcing TVS Motor's 
positioning in the national market. 
 
About TVS Motor Company 
 
TVS Motor Company (BSE:532343 and NSE: TVSMOTOR), part of TVS VENU, is a reputed two and 
three-wheeler manufacturer globally, championing progress through sustainable mobility with four 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities located in India and Indonesia. Rooted in our 100-year legacy 
of trust, value, and passion for customers, it takes pride in making internationally accepted products of 
the highest quality through innovative and sustainable processes. TVS Motor is the only two-wheeler 
company to have won the prestigious Deming Prize. Our products lead in their respective categories in 
the J.D. Power IQS and APEAL surveys. We have been ranked No. 1 Company in the J.D. Power 
Customer Service Satisfaction Survey for four consecutive years. Our group company Norton 
Motorcycles, based in the United Kingdom, is one of the most emotive motorcycle brands in the world. 
TVS Motor Company endeavours to deliver the most superior customer experience across 90 countries 
in which we operate.  
 
For more information, please visit www.tvsmotor.com   
 
For further details, please contact: 
Kanika Mehta: kanika.mehta@tvsmotor.com
---

HDFC Mutual Fund: SEBI Registration Number: MF/044/00/6  
 
HDFC Mutual Fund Enters the SIF Space with H-SIF to Unlock New Investment 
Opportunities for India’s Evolving Investors 
Launches H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund as its first investment strategy 
NFO Period: November 13, 2026, to November 27, 2026 
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: HDFC Mutual Fund, one of India’s leading mutual fund houses, today 
announced its entry into the Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) space with the launch of H-SIF, its SIF 
platform. Its first investment strategy, the H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, is an interval investment 
strategy investing in equity and debt securities, including limited short exposure in equity and debt 
through derivatives. The New Fund Offer (NFO) will open on November 13, 2026, and close on 
November 27, 2026. 
H-SIF draws on the foundation HDFC Mutual Fund has built over more than 25 years. Today, the fund 
house serves over 1.75 crore unique investors and has a presence across mutual funds, portfolio 
management services, alternatives and international business through GIFT City. H-SIF will be guided 
by the same disciplined investment approach, in-depth research and risk framework that underpin 
these businesses. 
HDFC Mutual Fund’s entry comes at a time when investors are navigating heightened uncertainty. 
Indian equity markets have been volatile through 2026, with sharp corrections in March and again in 
September, when the Nifty 50 recorded its steepest monthly fall since March. Such phases tend to 
weigh on sentiment and make it harder for investors to stay invested. At the same time, investors are 
increasingly looking beyond traditional products for solutions that can help them participate in 
markets while managing risk. This is reflected in the growth of the SIF category, where assets have 
risen from about ₹2,010 crore in October 2025 to ₹38,287 crore in September 2026, according to AMFI, 
with hybrid long-short strategies attracting the largest share. 
Commenting on the launch, Mr. Navneet Munot, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, 
HDFC Asset Management Company Limited, said, “Investors have placed their trust in HDFC Mutual 
Fund through many market cycles, with several of our funds completing more than three decades, and 
that trust shapes how we approach every new offering. SIFs can provide investors access to 
sophisticated strategies within a transparent and well-regulated framework. As investor needs evolve, 
we launch H-SIF our Specialized Investment Fund platform backed by our emphasis on risk 
management and a team with deep experience across equities, derivatives and fixed income. With H-
SIF, our endeavour is to offer investors a new way to participate in India’s growth, guided by the same 
discipline that has defined our journey so far.” 
The H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, positioned as an Arbitrage+ strategy. It is proposed to be built 
around a stable core of high degree of safety debt papers, arbitrage and REITs/InvITs, which aims to 
provide a relatively steady return profile. Around this core, the fund proposes to use derivative 
strategies primarily to manage risk, such as hedging positions, earning option premiums and taking 
limited short positions of up to 25% of net assets. Selective participation in corporate events such as 
IPOs, buybacks, open offers and mergers provides further opportunities for returns. Rather than 
relying on the direction of the market, the approach seeks to generate returns from interest income, 

 
 
HDFC Mutual Fund: SEBI Registration Number: MF/044/00/6  
 
arbitrage spreads, option premiums and tactical allocation to special situations. The strategy is suited 
to flat, mildly rising and volatile markets, with a preferred investment horizon of more than 18 months. 
Explaining the approach, Mr. Paul S Parampreet, Fund Manager- Equities, HDFC Asset Management 
Company Limited, said, “Periods of volatility tend to make investors hesitant, but they can also create 
opportunities for a strategy designed to use them. Our focus is on building a portfolio that does not 
rely on a single source of return. While the core exposure is meant to anchor the portfolio, derivatives 
would allow us to manage risk actively and endeavour to benefit when volatility is elevated. We will 
remain selective and disciplined in the positions we take, with the aim of offering investors a relatively 
steady experience over their investment horizon.” 
The strategy will be managed by Mr. Paul S Parampreet and Mr. Ihab Dalwai (Equity), Mr. Anil Bamboli 
(Debt) and Mr. Gopal Agrawal (Overseas Investments), bringing together experience across equities, 
derivatives and fixed income. 
The minimum investment in the strategy is ₹10 lakh across SIF strategies at the PAN level, while 
accredited investors can invest a minimum of ₹10,000, subject to applicable conditions. Subscriptions 
will be available daily and redemptions twice a week, on Mondays and Wednesdays. An exit load of 
0.5% will apply to units redeemed or switched out within 90 days of allotment, with no exit load 
thereafter. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
#Investors should consult their financial advisers if in doubt about whether the product is suitable for them. 
 
For more information, refer product literature at https://hsif.hdfcfund.com/ 
This investment strategy is proposed to be listed on NSE and /or BSE. NSE and BSE Disclaimer: It is to be distinctly 
understood that the permission given by National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE)/ BSE Limited (BSE) 
should not in any way be deemed or construed that the Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) has 
been cleared or approved by NSE/ BSE nor does it certify the correctness or completeness of any of the contents 
of the ISID. The investors are advised to refer to the ISID for the full text of the Disclaimer clause of NSE/ BSE.  
HDFC Bank (Sponsor of HDFC Mutual Fund) is not liable or responsible for any loss or shortfall resulting from the 
operations of the Investment Strategy. 
Investments in Specialized Investment Fund involves relatively higher risk including potential loss of 
capital, liquidity risk and market volatility. Please read all investment strategy related documents 
carefully before making the investment decision.

HDFC Mutual Fund Enters the SIF Space with H-SIF to Unlock New Investment 
Opportunities for India’s Evolving Investors 
Launches H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund as its first investment strategy 
NFO Period: November 13, 2026, to November 27, 2026 
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: HDFC Mutual Fund, one of India’s leading mutual fund houses, today 
announced its entry into the Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) space with the launch of H-SIF, its SIF 
platform. Its first investment strategy, the H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, is an interval investment 
strategy investing in equity and debt securities, including limited short exposure in equity and debt 
through derivatives. The New Fund Offer (NFO) will open on November 13, 2026, and close on 
November 27, 2026. 
H-SIF draws on the foundation HDFC Mutual Fund has built over more than 25 years. Today, the fund 
house serves over 1.75 crore unique investors and has a presence across mutual funds, portfolio 
management services, alternatives and international business through GIFT City. H-SIF will be guided 
by the same disciplined investment approach, in-depth research and risk framework that underpin 
these businesses. 
HDFC Mutual Fund’s entry comes at a time when investors are navigating heightened uncertainty. 
Indian equity markets have been volatile through 2026, with sharp corrections in March and again in 
September, when the Nifty 50 recorded its steepest monthly fall since March. Such phases tend to 
weigh on sentiment and make it harder for investors to stay invested. At the same time, investors are 
increasingly looking beyond traditional products for solutions that can help them participate in 
markets while managing risk. This is reflected in the growth of the SIF category, where assets have 
risen from about ₹2,010 crore in October 2025 to ₹38,287 crore in September 2026, according to AMFI, 
with hybrid long-short strategies attracting the largest share. 
Commenting on the launch, Mr. Navneet Munot, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, 
HDFC Asset Management Company Limited, said, “Investors have placed their trust in HDFC Mutual 
Fund through many market cycles, with several of our funds completing more than three decades, and 
that trust shapes how we approach every new offering. SIFs can provide investors access to 
sophisticated strategies within a transparent and well-regulated framework. As investor needs evolve, 
we launch H-SIF our Specialized Investment Fund platform backed by our emphasis on risk 
management and a team with deep experience across equities, derivatives and fixed income. With H-
SIF, our endeavour is to offer investors a new way to participate in India’s growth, guided by the same 
discipline that has defined our journey so far.” 
The H-SIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, positioned as an Arbitrage+ strategy. It is proposed to be built 
around a stable core of high degree of safety debt papers, arbitrage and REITs/InvITs, which aims to 
provide a relatively steady return profile. Around this core, the fund proposes to use derivative 
strategies primarily to manage risk, such as hedging positions, earning option premiums and taking 
limited short positions of up to 25% of net assets. Selective participation in corporate events such as 
IPOs, buybacks, open offers and mergers provides further opportunities for returns. Rather than 
relying on the direction of the market, the approach seeks to generate returns from interest income, 

 
 
HDFC Mutual Fund: SEBI Registration Number: MF/044/00/6  
 
arbitrage spreads, option premiums and tactical allocation to special situations. The strategy is suited 
to flat, mildly rising and volatile markets, with a preferred investment horizon of more than 18 months. 
Explaining the approach, Mr. Paul S Parampreet, Fund Manager- Equities, HDFC Asset Management 
Company Limited, said, “Periods of volatility tend to make investors hesitant, but they can also create 
opportunities for a strategy designed to use them. Our focus is on building a portfolio that does not 
rely on a single source of return. While the core exposure is meant to anchor the portfolio, derivatives 
would allow us to manage risk actively and endeavour to benefit when volatility is elevated. We will 
remain selective and disciplined in the positions we take, with the aim of offering investors a relatively 
steady experience over their investment horizon.” 
The strategy will be managed by Mr. Paul S Parampreet and Mr. Ihab Dalwai (Equity), Mr. Anil Bamboli 
(Debt) and Mr. Gopal Agrawal (Overseas Investments), bringing together experience across equities, 
derivatives and fixed income. 
The minimum investment in the strategy is ₹10 lakh across SIF strategies at the PAN level, while 
accredited investors can invest a minimum of ₹10,000, subject to applicable conditions. Subscriptions 
will be available daily and redemptions twice a week, on Mondays and Wednesdays. An exit load of 
0.5% will apply to units redeemed or switched out within 90 days of allotment, with no exit load 
thereafter. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
#Investors should consult their financial advisers if in doubt about whether the product is suitable for them. 
 
For more information, refer product literature at https://hsif.hdfcfund.com/ 
This investment strategy is proposed to be listed on NSE and /or BSE. NSE and BSE Disclaimer: It is to be distinctly 
understood that the permission given by National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE)/ BSE Limited (BSE) 
should not in any way be deemed or construed that the Investment Strategy Information Document (ISID) has 
been cleared or approved by NSE/ BSE nor does it certify the correctness or completeness of any of the contents 
of the ISID. The investors are advised to refer to the ISID for the full text of the Disclaimer clause of NSE/ BSE.  
HDFC Bank (Sponsor of HDFC Mutual Fund) is not liable or responsible for any loss or shortfall resulting from the 
operations of the Investment Strategy. 
Investments in Specialized Investment Fund involves relatively higher risk including potential loss of 
capital, liquidity risk and market volatility. Please read all investment strategy related documents 
carefully before making the investment decision.

Press Release  
Indore, November 13, 2026 
 
Godrej Properties adds ~31-acre land parcel in Indore for plotted development  
Godrej Properties Ltd. (GPL) (BSE scrip id: GODREJPROP), one of India’s leading real estate 
developers, today announced the addition of a ~31-acre land parcel on Indore-Ujjain Road, 
Indore. The land is planned for a ploŊed residential development with an estimated saleable 
area of ~0.7 million square feet.  
The transaction strengthens GPL’s presence in Indore and expands its footprint in the micro-
market. The company already has two plotted developments in the city, Godrej Greenview 
Estate and Verdania Estate, both of which have witnessed strong customer demand and are at 
an advanced stage of completion. 
Indore-Ujjain Road continues to be one of the city’s fastest-growing residential corridors, with 
easy access to Indore International Airport, Ujjain city and key commercial centres, along with 
well-established schools and hospitals. The planned expansion of the metro network, the 
growth of the corporate and IT sector and continued infrastructure development have 
strengthened Indore’s residential market. Within this market, demand for plotted homes has 
risen steadily as buyers seek more space and the freedom to design their own homes.  
Gaurav Pandey, MD & CEO, Godrej Properties, said, “Indore is one of India’s most promising real 
estate markets, and we see significant long-term potential here. Located on Indore-Ujjain Road, the 
land gives us the opportunity to create a thoughtfully planned community and build on the 
momentum of our existing projects. This is our third project in the city and reflects our commitment 
to creating value for customers in high-growth markets, where demand for well-planned, branded 
plotted communities continues to rise.” 
The proposed development will oňer residential plots of varying sizes, supported by planned 
infrastructure, recreational spaces and premium amenities.

Godrej Properties adds ~31-acre land parcel in Indore for plotted development  
Godrej Properties Ltd. (GPL) (BSE scrip id: GODREJPROP), one of India’s leading real estate 
developers, today announced the addition of a ~31-acre land parcel on Indore-Ujjain Road, 
Indore. The land is planned for a ploŊed residential development with an estimated saleable 
area of ~0.7 million square feet.  
The transaction strengthens GPL’s presence in Indore and expands its footprint in the micro-
market. The company already has two plotted developments in the city, Godrej Greenview 
Estate and Verdania Estate, both of which have witnessed strong customer demand and are at 
an advanced stage of completion. 
Indore-Ujjain Road continues to be one of the city’s fastest-growing residential corridors, with 
easy access to Indore International Airport, Ujjain city and key commercial centres, along with 
well-established schools and hospitals. The planned expansion of the metro network, the 
growth of the corporate and IT sector and continued infrastructure development have 
strengthened Indore’s residential market. Within this market, demand for plotted homes has 
risen steadily as buyers seek more space and the freedom to design their own homes.  
Gaurav Pandey, MD & CEO, Godrej Properties, said, “Indore is one of India’s most promising real 
estate markets, and we see significant long-term potential here. Located on Indore-Ujjain Road, the 
land gives us the opportunity to create a thoughtfully planned community and build on the 
momentum of our existing projects. This is our third project in the city and reflects our commitment 
to creating value for customers in high-growth markets, where demand for well-planned, branded 
plotted communities continues to rise.” 
The proposed development will oňer residential plots of varying sizes, supported by planned 
infrastructure, recreational spaces and premium amenities.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Sansera Engineering Limited Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. This conference call may contain forward-looking statements about 
the company, which are based on the beliefs, opinions, and expectations of the company as on 
date of this call. These statements are not the guarantees of future performance and involve risks 
and uncertainties that are difficult to predict. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be on the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star 0 on your touch-tone 
phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. B. R. Preetham, Joint Managing Director and Group 
CEO. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
B. R. Preetham: 
Thank you, and good morning, everyone. I would like to take this opportunity to wish everyone 
a very happy and prosperous Diwali. Joining me on this call today are my colleagues, our CFO, 
Mr. Vikas Goel, our CEO of ADS division, Mr. Hari Krishnan, our CEO of our automotive 
division, Mr. Rahul Kale, and head of our corporate strategy, Mr. Praveen Chauhan, along with 
SGA, our investor relation advisors. 
Our results and the investor presentations are available on the stock exchanges and on our 
website, and I trust you have had a chance to review them. I am pleased to report another strong 
quarter for Sansera, with the highest ever quarterly revenue of INR10,915 million, up 32% year-
on-year. EBITDA stood at INR2,112 million, registering a year-on-year growth of 48%, while 
PAT stood at INR1,086 million with a Y-o-Y growth of 52%. 
EBITDA and PAT margin for the quarter were recorded at 19.4% and 10% respectively. For H1 
FY 2027, revenue was INR21,127 million, up 33% year-on-year, with EBITDA of INR4,073 
million and PAT of INR1,960 million. We delivered this performance against a tougher cost 
backdrop. The renewed conflict in West Asia led to an increase in cost across several categories, 
including cutting tools, freight, and logistics. 
Additionally, the revision in minimum wages in Karnataka added to the cost pressures, further 
impacting our margins. Even so, we held our margins, strong revenue growth, and a rising 
contribution from the ADS business and the benefits of operating leverage allowed us to absorb 
these cost pressures and protect our profitability. What is most encouraging is that our growth 
continues to be broad-based, with healthy performance across most of our businesses. 
This is a clear sign of how far we have come in building Sansera into a diversified company with 
multiple growth engines, and our non-automotive business has been a center to this 
transformation. Auto ICE now accounts for about 65% of our sales on a much larger base, 
broadly in line with the target we set ourselves at the time of our IPO. 
We are now very close to realizing that vision and an important milestone in Sansera's journey 
that sets us up well for the next phase of sustainable growth. Importantly, we have achieved this 

 
Sansera Engineering Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
while our core Auto ICE business continues to grow at a healthy pace, with sustained 
momentum. The change in mix is driven by the faster growth of our newer businesses, not by 
any slowdown in our core automotive operations. 
This balanced portfolio makes us more resilient, broadens our access to growth opportunities, 
and positions Sansera to deliver sustainable growth over the long term. We see this as the 
beginning, not the end of our diversification journey. We will continue to add new sectors, new 
customers, deepen our wallet share with existing ones, and move up the value chain. Let me now 
take you through the performance of our individual businesses. 
Let me begin with our core Auto ICE, which recorded a quarterly sales of INR6,697 million, up 
18% year-on-year. The growth was broad-based, with passenger vehicles, two-wheeler 
motorcycles, scooters each posting their highest ever quarterly sales. Our Auto-Tech Agnostic 
and xEV business also delivered their best-ever quarter in terms of sales and combined sales of 
INR1,363 million. 
Adding to our growth pipeline, commercial production at the Sansera-Nichidai JV is expected 
to commence towards the end of H2 FY 2027. October marked a milestone for the industry, with 
domestic passenger vehicle wholesale crossing 5 lakh units in a single month for the very first 
time. Elevated order backlogs and lean dealer inventories, with demand still running ahead of 
the supply, give us good visibility into quarter three FY 2027. We are also seeing strong demand 
for premium technologically advanced vehicles. 
Together with rising EV adoption, these trends are steadily increasing the engineered content 
per vehicle. Export demand remains strong as global customers continue to diversify their supply 
chain. Indian manufacturers with proven quality standards, process design capabilities, and 
manufacturing scale, with manufacturing scale are increasingly preferred, giving us room to 
deepen our customer relationships and expand our wallet share. 
At the same time, OEMs with a manufacturing base in India are seeing strong export demand, 
which is a clear tailwind for auto components suppliers like Sansera. Overall, with festive 
momentum carrying into the second half, our automotive business is well-placed to benefit from 
the healthy domestic demand, rising technology adoption, and diversification of global supply 
chains. 
Our order book as on September 30, 2026, which is the peak annual revenues of the sale of new 
businesses, excluding ADS, stands at INR22,410 million. Moving to our non-automotive 
business, ADS continued to be a key growth driver within the segment. Revenue for Q2 FY 
2027 stood at INR1,643 million, taking half-yearly revenue to INR3,097 million. This reflects 
growing scale of the business and the rising opportunities across industries. 
During the quarter, the non-automotive segment posted its record sales for the quarter, crossing 
INR2,000 million mark and contributing 20.9% of total sales. At quarter end, our cumulative 
unexecuted lifetime order book backlog for ADS business executable over next five years stood 
at INR58.7 billion, giving us strong revenue visibility. 

 
Sansera Engineering Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
ADS remains a powerful growth engine for Sansera, backed by robust industry demand and a 
healthy order book. In aerospace, global OEMs increasingly see India as a strategic sourcing 
hub, opening the door for us to move up in the higher value chain, more complex components 
and sub-assemblies. In semiconductor, we are expanding our product portfolio and exploring 
new avenues for customer diversification as well. In defense, our dedicated facility is expected 
to begin operations towards the end of Q3 FY 2027, further strengthening our ability to capture 
emerging opportunities. 
With the new SKUs coming on stream in the ADS business in H2 FY 2027, we expect a strong 
growth catalyst that should accelerate our momentum through the second half. These initiatives 
remain central to building a larger, more diversified, and higher value ADS business in the years 
ahead. Looking ahead, we remain confident in our growth outlook, supported by healthy demand 
across our automotive and non-automotive businesses, rising premiumization, electrification, 
and a favorable realignment of global supply chains. With our strong engineering capabilities, 
longstanding customer relationships, and continued investments in capacity and technology, we 
are well-positioned to capitalize on these opportunities and sustain our growth momentum in the 
years ahead. With this, 
I would now like to hand over to our CFO, Mr. Vikas Goel, to take this presentation forward. 
Vikas. 
Vikas Goel: 
Thank you, Preetham, and good morning, everyone. Let me walk you through our second quarter 
numbers. Three themes stand out as we look at this quarter. Profits grew faster than the revenue, 
margins expanded despite cost headwinds, and our balance sheet continues to fund growth, 
backed by a strong order book. Our revenue grew 32% year-on-year to record INR10,915 
million, with growth across all our businesses. 
Gross margin expanded by 180 basis points to 43% on a favorable product mix. Employee costs 
rose 25% to INR1,469 million, slower than the revenue, and include a provision of INR167 
million for the Karnataka minimum wage revision. We continue to monitor the Labour Codes 
for any further impact, and we will keep you updated on this. Other expenses rose 41% to 
INR1,114 million on higher scale and freight costs. 
EBITDA crossed INR2,000 million mark for the first time at INR2,112 million, up 48%. The 
margin expanded by about 200 basis points year-on-year and 15 basis points sequentially to 
19.4% on our richer mix and operating leverage. Other income was INR116 million versus 
INR116 million last year. 
Depreciation rose 20% to INR602 million, and finance cost to INR146 million from INR81 
million, reflecting our expanded asset base and higher borrowing cost for capex and working 
capital. Profit after tax rose 52% to INR1,086 million, a margin of 10%. Let me briefly cover 
the half-yearly numbers. For the first half, revenue grew 33% to INR21,127 million, and 
EBITDA grew 48% to INR4,073 million, with margin up 200 basis points to 19.3%. 
` 
Reported profit after tax grew 46% to INR1,960 million, a 9.3% margin, excluding the Q1 
litigation settlement of INR169 million. Or INR127 million post-tax normalized. The 

 
Sansera Engineering Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 18 
 
normalized PAT was INR2,087 million. Moving to balance sheet and cash flow and net debt. In 
H1, we generated operating cash flow of INR2,073 million. 
Against this, an investment was made of about INR3,260 million in the Capex for automotive 
and ADS business. INR300 million was invested in our joint venture with Nichidai. Together, 
these investments exceeded operating cash flow by about INR1,487 million, contributing to 
increase in the net debt. Working capital rose to INR8,544 million at the end of September from 
INR7,359 million in March, mainly due to higher revenue share from ADS business, meaning 
inventory support and further increased volumes. This represents about 19.6% of the annualized 
Q2 revenue. 
Net debt rose by about INR2,000 million to INR2,612 million at the end of September from 
INR604 million in March, as we invested in growth. Leverage remains conservative at about 0.3 
x of the annualized EBITDA for H1, with ample headroom to fund our plans. This investment 
is backed by strong order wins. Our ADS backlog rose from INR58.7 billion from INR44.4 
billion in June, including a large multi-year semiconductor order. 
Separately, our non-ADS business order book measured at peak annual sales rose to INR22.4 
billion from INR18.5 billion. To deliver these orders, we have raised FY27 Capex projection to 
INR8,000 million, fased with the customer validations, while keeping firm discipline on working 
capital, cash and leverage. In closing, with momentum across all our businesses and a strong 
balance, we are well-positioned for the next phase of profitable growth. 
With this, we conclude our opening remarks and open the floor for questions.

PAT stood at INR1,086 million with a Y-o-Y growth of 52%.

million and PAT of INR1,960 million. We delivered this performance against a tougher cost 
backdrop. The renewed conflict in West Asia led to an increase in cost across several categories, 
including cutting tools, freight, and logistics.

impacting our margins. Even so, we held our margins, strong revenue growth, and a rising 
contribution from the ADS business and the benefits of operating leverage allowed us to absorb 
these cost pressures and protect our profitability. What is most encouraging is that our growth 
continues to be broad-based, with healthy performance across most of our businesses.

multiple growth engines, and our non-automotive business has been a center to this 
transformation. Auto ICE now accounts for about 65% of our sales on a much larger base, 
broadly in line with the target we set ourselves at the time of our IPO.

that sets us up well for the next phase of sustainable growth. Importantly, we have achieved this

unexecuted lifetime order book backlog for ADS business executable over next five years stood 
at INR58.7 billion, giving us strong revenue visibility.
