Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Aditya Infotech Q2 FY2027 conference call 
hosted by ICICI Securities Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only 
mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. 
Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star 
then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Aniruddha Joshi from ICICI Securities. Thank you, and 
over to you. 
Aniruddha Joshi: 
Yes, thanks, Iqra. On behalf of ICICI Securities, we welcome you all to Q2 FY2027 and H1 
FY2027 results conference call of Aditya Infotech Limited. We have with us today senior 
management represented by Mr. Aditya Khemka, Managing Director, Mr. Anup Nair, Director, 
Strategy, Business Development, and Investor Relations, Mr. Yogesh Sharma, Chief Financial 
Officer, and Ms. Dipika Dubey, Manager, Investor Relations. 
 
Now I hand over the call to the senior management for taking us through the quarterly 
performance, and then we will open the floor for question-and-answer session. Thanks, and over 
to you, Aditya ji. 
Aditya Khemka: 
Yes, thank you, Aniruddha. Good day, everyone. Wish you a very happy Dhanteras and thank 
you for joining us today for Aditya Infotech's Q2 and H1 FY2027 earnings call. With me are 
our CFO and our Investor Relations team. The results and the investor presentation are on the 
Stock Exchange websites and also on our company website. 
Let me start with the headline. This has been the strongest half in our history. In quarter two, 
revenue was INR 1,746 crores, up 89.9% year-on-year. EBITDA was INR 307 crores, up 177%, 
with a margin of 17.6%. PAT before the exceptional item was INR 220 crores, up 214%. For 
the first half year, revenue was INR 3,148 crores, up 89.7%. EBITDA was INR 515 crores at a 
16.3 margin. PAT before the exceptional item was INR 362 crores, up 252%. 
Also, sequentially, quarter two revenue grew 24.5% over quarter one, and EBITDA margin rose 
from 14.8% to 17.6%. Reported PAT for quarter two was INR 185.5 crores after a one-time 
exceptional item of INR 34.4 crores from a fire incident that happened in our Kadapa plant due 
to short circuit in September. 
The loss is fully covered by insurance, and the claim has already been lodged. Excluding it, the 
underlying business delivered the INR 220 crores PAT, which I just mentioned. CP PLUS 
remains the core engine of this growth. It contributed about 88% of revenue in quarter two 
against 86% a year ago. 
Within CP PLUS, IP products are now about 79% of the portfolio, up from 71%. Our leadership 
in the Indian video surveillance has widened. In the 12 months to September 2026, our share of 
the total market, including the unorganized segment, was about 42%, which at the time of our 
IPO was 30%. 

Aditya Infotech Limited 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 13 
 
The industry's move to higher data security standards as well as trusted supply chains played to 
our strengths. Cybersecurity-certified products needed scale in manufacturing, depth in R&D, 
and a secure supply of critical components. They needed the nationwide reach to put products 
in the market across India and an Indian brand which the Indian consumers can trust. 
They also needed the most experienced management and field teams in the Indian surveillance 
ecosystem. We had all these ingredients in place, and the gains eventually came from our team's 
execution. We expect to keep gaining market share through the rest of the year. On our revised 
guidance, our FY2027 share is expected to be in the range of 43% to 45%. 
On the margin side, our gross margin for the first half was 30.4%, up 374 basis points year-on-
year. Three things drove it: a richer brand and product mix, deeper localization initiatives, and 
operating leverage. In Q2, gross margin was 30%, flat year-on-year, and slightly below Q1, 
30.8%, as we began absorbing part of the input cost increase in SOC and memory. 
I want to highlight clearly about the input cost environment. Critical semiconductor components 
like SOC, DDR, and flash prices have risen sharply across the electronics industry. Ahead of 
this, we took strategic positions in SOC and memory, which is why inventory is on the higher 
side on our balance sheet. 
This was a planned move, as this protected both our consistent supply situation as well as our 
margins in the first half year. We strategically passed on the input cost increases rather gradually 
to market instead of all at once. As market leaders, we did not want to give the channel a sudden 
price shock and ensured that the momentum of overall market expansion as well as our market 
share growth continues. 
As the lower-cost inventories gets used up, and as we moderate price increases to further gain 
market share, we expect second-half margins to be lower than Q2. Thus, Q2 should not be read 
as the run rate. That is why we are keeping our full-year EBITDA margin guidance at 14%-
15%, even after a 16.3% in the first half, so as to keep enough cushion to support our market 
share growth strategy in such a volatile input cost environment. 
In September, we completed our qualified institutions placement and raised INR 1,500 crores. 
Leading domestic and global institutions took part, and I thank them once again for their 
confidence in the company and management. In October, we repaid all our borrowings, and now 
the company is debt free. 
The lower finance cost will show from the second half. The proceeds will go to three users as 
set out in the placement document: repaying borrowings of Aditya Infotech Limited and also 
our wholly owned subsidiary, AIL Dixon, manufacturing capacity expansion through our 
wholly owned subsidiary, inorganic growth through acquisitions, and general corporate 
purposes. 
On 30th September, cash and cash equivalents were INR 1,434 crores against borrowing of INR 
363 crores. Annualized return on equity for the first half was 26.9%. Also, the finance cost was 

Aditya Infotech Limited 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 13 
 
down 41% year-on-year for first half year. 
Working capital went up in the half mainly due to increase in inventory because of strategic 
component buying that I described to maintain supply strength. It was a deliberate choice to 
secure supply and cost. Collections have improved. Receivable days came down to 87 in Q2 
from 93 in Q1 and 105 a year ago. 
As the components positions get used up, working capital should come down in future. Our 
board approved, and we signed agreements to invest INR 45.4 crores for a 30% stake on a fully 
diluted basis in BLUE KGraph AI Solutions. BLUE has built a video compression layer that 
works on top of standard H.264. 
It can cut storage and bandwidth by up to 90%, needs no GPU, and works with cameras already 
installed in the field. The six highly talented co-founders have built and sold a video analytics 
company already before. For us, this means lower storage costs in our NVRs and cloud, and a 
recurring software layer on our installed base. 
We will hold one board seat and one observer seat, and completion is subject to customary 
conditions. On the manufacturing side, our Kadapa plant capacity is at 2.5 million units a month, 
and we plan to more than double this through Kadapa phase 3 and a new facility in Greater 
Noida, funded from the QIP. 
We are also localizing four components’ categories: lenses, cables, housing enclosures and IoT 
modules. Our fully integrated lens plant is planned in Greater Noida with a capacity of 2 million 
lenses per month. The housing and enclosures plant in Kadapa begins trials this quarter, with 
commercial production coming in place from the coming quarter. 
The cable plant will also go live in Q4 of this financial year, which is next quarter. Localization 
improves quality, secures supply, and adds to margins over time as we scale this up. Through 
our multi brand strategy, we now have a portfolio that addresses every segment of the market, 
from entry level to the most premium enterprise. 
CP PLUS is our flagship and mainstream brand. The new range of CP PLUS PRO series targets 
the premium enterprise segment, and its rollout is planned in the Q4 of FY2027. The other two 
brands, NEXIVUE and EYRA, serves to the entry and the mid-market, and this counters the 
lower end of the pyramid as well as the unorganized sector. 
This festive season, we launched a national campaign with Bollywood superstar Ranveer Singh 
as our brand ambassador. It ran alongside our presence in the Indian cricket space as well as 
major airports, and it builds awareness of intelligent security in everyday life. On the back of a 
strong first half, we are raising our FY2027 guidance. 
Revenue, we are raising it to INR 6,500 crores, INR 6,800 crores, up from INR 6,000 crores, 
INR 6,500 crores, which is a growth of 54% to 61% over the year. EBITDA margins, we are 
maintaining still at 14%-15%, while the PAT margin we are now raising now to 9% to 10%,

STQC certifications backlogs held back supply across the industry. The second half of last year 
was a normal base, so growth will normalize from these levels while still remaining strong, as

To sum up, we have widened our market leadership, strengthened our balance sheet, and are 
investing in capacity, localization, and technology. Our focus remains on disciplined execution

operating leverage. In Q2, gross margin was 30%, flat year-on-year, and slightly below Q1,

What we are trying to do is ensure, like CP PLUS always stood about taking CCTV to the 
masses. Our strategy here itself is whether we can take cloud storage and AI analytics to a mass 
level. For that, of course, the pricing becomes important. We are first building the capabilities 
on the cloud and price points where it can lead to mass adoption. 
The second part of your question was the export market. Yes, again, I would like to say that 
depending on the country, we would have the complete product range, as you can see. As we 
build up the more product range, the CP PLUS PRO and more professional cameras and the 
manufacturing capacity, we would have the ability to target whichever segment where there is 
an opportunity in the international market. 
But it is a bit too early to again talk about which segments and which markets we will be 
entering, since it is a slightly longer timeframe, 18 to 24. Maybe we will discuss that sometime 
in the future. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
Sure. Just a quick follow up to that. I understand that it is early to explain about the export 
market and who are we competing here, but does it really require an establishment of distribution 
presence like we have in the domestic market? 
Anup Nair: 
Yes and no. Santosh, again, we have not spelt out our strategy for those markets. It can be a mix 
of our own brand, maybe it can be a partnership with somebody, it can be an inorganic. So, it 
depends on what we are doing. Maybe we will be open to doing ODM for somebody else in 
those market as a market entry. So, it depends on how we plan it out. What we are clear on, 
basis our initial assessment, is there is an opportunity, and that we have studied. Now, how we 
go about executing that, I think it will still need some more time for us to lay it out to you. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
Thank you very much, sir. All the very best for us.

Hi, very good afternoon. Thank you so much for the opportunity. So, three questions. Firstly, 
we have all gone through very hyper growth this year, and hence we all struggle to figure out 
what is the most sustainable growth rate and margins for this industry and for CP PLUS. If I just 
take a bit more medium-term outlook, not the second half, and look at FY 2028, FY 2029 fiscals, 
you will end market share at 45%, what you said, by March 2027, roughly thereabouts. 
Next two years, given that most of the pricing hike is done, your revenue growth should reflect 
volume growth. That is one understanding. And second is, because you are backward 
integrating, there should be some benefit flowing through on your EBITDA margins. If I take a 
three-year view, sir, could you please give us some color that how should this revenue growth 
rate, should it be equal to volume growth rate going forward? And then how much benefit would 
you expect over a two-to-three-year timeframe if your backward integration plays out on time?

Rahul, let us answer that first question since it's a long question. Thanks for pointing out where

You've seen the figure where we are estimating the market at. From a unit growth perspective, 
we still see that from a three- to five-year horizon, there should be a CAGR of 18%-20% on unit 
terms. Now, coming to your second question, how does that translate into value? That depends 
upon the price rise, which I think is a $100 million question nobody can answer, whether when 
will the price rise taper on both SOC and memory. 
That's a difficult question to answer. But again, taking a view on that, the price rises are still 
going up. Maybe the rate of price increase will slow down. Maybe in the near term, the next 
year or onwards, the value growth should be much higher than unit growth still. Our endeavour 
has always been to beat the market growth rate.

To the Board of Directors of Usha Martin Limited 
1. 
We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of consolidated unaudited financial results of Usha 
Martin Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'the Holding Company' ) which includes Usha Martin 
Employees Welfare Trust ('the trust') and its subsidiaries (the Holding Company and its subsidiaries 
together referred to as the 'Group') and its share of the net profit after tax and total comprehensive 
income of its joint ventures for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and the year to date results 
for the period from April 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026 ('the Statement' ) attached herewith, 
being submitted by the Holding Company pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 33 of the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, as amended ('the Regulations'). 
2. 
This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Holding Company's Management and approved by 
the Holding Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition 
and measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34 'Interim Financial 
Reporting' prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ( 'the Act') read with relevant 
rules issued thereunder ('Ind AS 34' ) and other recognised accounting principles generally accepted 
in India and is in compliance with the Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on 
the Statement based on our review. 
3. 
We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements 
(SRE) 2410, 'Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the 
Entity' issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial 
information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and 
accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially 
less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing specified under 
section 143(10) of the Act and consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would 
become aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not 
express an audit opinion. 
We also performed procedures in accordance with the circular issued by the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India under Regulation 33 (8) of the Regulations, to the extent applicable.

Edelweiss reports Consolidated PAT (Post MI) growth of 50% YoY to INR 193 Cr  
Robust Profitability * Growing Customer Franchise * Strong Balance Sheet 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Six months ended September 26 Highlights 
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 315 Cr, up 61% YoY 
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 5,021 Cr, up 20% YoY 
Quarter ended September 26 Highlights 
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 193 Cr, up 50% YoY 
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 2,602 Cr, up 37% YoY 
Robust growth in key metrics of operating businesses in the quarter 
 Alternative Asset Management Fee Paying AUM (FPAUM) grew by 28% YoY to INR 49,164 Cr  
 Mutual Fund business Equity AUM increased 40% YoY to INR 1,07,600 Cr; SIP Book reached INR 618 Cr, up 26% 
YoY  
 Asset Reconstruction business recovered INR 1,387 Cr in the quarter, up 13% YoY while INR 605 Cr of assets 
acquired in the same period, up 70% YoY 
 MSME loans of INR 560 Cr disbursed in the quarter, up 3x YoY 
 Gross Written Premium for General Insurance increased to INR 366 Cr, up 40% YoY; the business turned 
profitable this quarter with profit after tax recorded at INR 5 Cr 
 Life Insurance recorded a Gross Premium of INR 558 Cr in the quarter, up 11% YoY; AUM increased by 13% YoY 
to INR 11,067 Cr  
Key Focus areas for FY27  
 
Listing of Edelweiss Alternatives – successfully completed its INR 1,200 Cr Initial Public Offering  
 
Carlyle came in as a strategic majority investor in Nido Home Finance – with an investment of ~INR 2,000 Cr  
 
Scaling up of profitability in Asset Management businesses – PAT for six months ended September grew by 
35% YoY for Alternative Asset Management and 64% YoY for Mutual Fund 
 
Insurance businesses on track to be profitable – Zuno turns profitable this quarter; combined losses for six 
months ended Sep reduced by 58% YoY  
 
Steady scale up in MSME business with 2x YoY growth in AUM and 3x YoY growth in disbursals for six months

Unaudited, Limited Reviewed Results Second Quarter Financial Year 2027  
Press Release, November 13, 2026 | www.edelweissfin.com  
 
 
Edelweiss reports Consolidated PAT (Post MI) growth of 50% YoY to INR 193 Cr  
Robust Profitability * Growing Customer Franchise * Strong Balance Sheet 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Six months ended September 26 Highlights 
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 315 Cr, up 61% YoY 
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 5,021 Cr, up 20% YoY 
Quarter ended September 26 Highlights 
 Consolidated PAT (Post MI) of INR 193 Cr, up 50% YoY 
 Consolidated Revenue of INR 2,602 Cr, up 37% YoY 
Robust growth in key metrics of operating businesses in the quarter 
 Alternative Asset Management Fee Paying AUM (FPAUM) grew by 28% YoY to INR 49,164 Cr  
 Mutual Fund business Equity AUM increased 40% YoY to INR 1,07,600 Cr; SIP Book reached INR 618 Cr, up 26% 
YoY  
 Asset Reconstruction business recovered INR 1,387 Cr in the quarter, up 13% YoY while INR 605 Cr of assets 
acquired in the same period, up 70% YoY 
 MSME loans of INR 560 Cr disbursed in the quarter, up 3x YoY 
 Gross Written Premium for General Insurance increased to INR 366 Cr, up 40% YoY; the business turned 
profitable this quarter with profit after tax recorded at INR 5 Cr 
 Life Insurance recorded a Gross Premium of INR 558 Cr in the quarter, up 11% YoY; AUM increased by 13% YoY 
to INR 11,067 Cr  
Key Focus areas for FY27  
 
Listing of Edelweiss Alternatives – successfully completed its INR 1,200 Cr Initial Public Offering  
 
Carlyle came in as a strategic majority investor in Nido Home Finance – with an investment of ~INR 2,000 Cr  
 
Scaling up of profitability in Asset Management businesses – PAT for six months ended September grew by 
35% YoY for Alternative Asset Management and 64% YoY for Mutual Fund 
 
Insurance businesses on track to be profitable – Zuno turns profitable this quarter; combined losses for six 
months ended Sep reduced by 58% YoY  
 
Steady scale up in MSME business with 2x YoY growth in AUM and 3x YoY growth in disbursals for six months 
ended Sep period 
Customer Franchise continues its growth trajectory 
 Our customer base remains on a steady growth trajectory, with customer reach up by 24% YoY to nearly 15 
million while customer assets witnessed an increase of 24% YoY to INR 2.9 Tn – demonstrating the continued 
trust reposed in us by our customers 
Resilient Balance Sheet with well capitalised businesses 
 Net Worth at INR 5,615 Cr 
 Consol Net Debt at INR 8,435 Cr, down 26% YoY 
 Corporate Net Debt declined by 18% YoY to INR 5,415 Cr  
 Independent operating businesses with capital adequacy of over 23% across credit entities  
 
 

 
 
 
 
      Edelweiss Financial Services Limited 
Unaudited, Limited Reviewed Results Second Quarter Financial Year 2027  
Press Release, November 13, 2026 | www.edelweissfin.com  
 
 
Speaking on the occasion, Rashesh Shah, Chairman, Edelweiss Financial Services Limited said: 
“India’s growth has remained resilient despite a challenging global environment. While geopolitical tensions and 
macroeconomic uncertainties continue to weigh on the global outlook, sustained public investment and healthy 
domestic demand continue to support the Indian economy. Rural demand remains resilient, while urban 
consumption is showing signs of gradual recovery. With continued policy support and strong domestic demand 
providing a firm foundation, India remains well placed to sustain its medium-term growth trajectory. 
At Edelweiss, in this quarter we reported a consolidated PAT (post MI) of INR 193 Cr, up 50% YoY. The businesses 
continued to demonstrate robust earnings growth with PAT in Alternative Asset Management at INR 88 Cr, up 27% 
YoY and Mutual Fund PAT at INR 37 Cr, up 114% YoY. Further, our balance sheet remained resilient as corporate net 
debt declined by 18% YoY. 
During the quarter, we remained on track and made meaningful progress on our key focus areas – Edelweiss 
Alternatives successfully completed its INR 1,200 Cr IPO and Carlyle is now a strategic majority investor in Nido Home 
Finance with an investment of ~INR 2,000 Cr. Our Asset Management businesses continued to scale strongly, while 
our Credit businesses witnessed a calibrated scale-up, with MSME disbursements growing threefold YoY in six 
months ended September. Our Insurance businesses are on track to be profitable with combined losses down by 
58% YoY in six months ended September; our General Insurance business, Zuno, turned profitable this quarter. These 
achievements reflect our focus on strengthening our businesses, maintaining robust balance sheet and creating long-
term value for all stakeholders.” 
 
Steady Performance across Businesses – Healthy metrics & Robust growth 
 
Alternative Asset Management:  
- Fee Paying AUM grew 28% YoY to INR 49,164 Cr and PAT for the quarter increased 27% YoY to INR 88 Cr 
- Annualized ROE improved to 29%, up ~270 bps YoY 
- Raised INR 8,000 Cr+ across Special Situations, Infra Yield and Private Equity strategies and INR 12,000 Cr+ in 
InvITs during six months ended Sep 
- Launched third flagship infrastructure fund, Infrastructure Yield Plus III (IYP III) 
 
Mutual Fund: 
- Equity AUM grew 40% YoY to INR 1,07,600 Cr; AUM grew 18% YoY to INR 1,83,200 Cr 
- Net equity inflows of INR 10,800 Cr, highest ever in a quarter, up 2.5x YoY 
- SIP book increased by 26% YoY to INR 618 Cr 
- Launched Altiva Equity Long – Short SIF; SIF AUM at INR 13,200 Cr 
 
Asset Reconstruction:  
- 
Acquired INR 605 Cr assets in the quarter, up 70% YoY 
- 
Recovered INR 1,387 Cr in the quarter, up 13% YoY 
- 
Share of retail assets in capital employed increased to 29% 
- 
Annualized RoE for the quarter at 18% 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
      Edelweiss Financial Services Limited 
Unaudited, Limited Reviewed Results Second Quarter Financial Year 2027  
Press Release, November 13, 2026 | www.edelweissfin.com  
 
 
NBFC: 
- 
MSME disbursals of INR 560 Cr in the quarter; tripled YoY 
- 
Portfolio continues to strengthen with GNPA at 2.10%, improved by 125 bps YoY  
- 
Wholesale SR wound down to zero from INR 18,000 Cr in Mar 19 
 
General Insurance: 
- Turned profitable this quarter, with PAT of INR 5 Cr 
- Gross written premium (GWP) increased by 40% YoY in the quarter; Motor accounted for 60% of GWP 
- Gross direct premium income (GDPI) increased by 41% YoY in the quarter vs. industry growth at 7% 
- Motor segment GDPI grew 66% YoY in the quarter vs. industry growth at 12% 
 
Life Insurance: 
- Gross premium of INR 558 Cr in the quarter, up 11% YoY 
- Total AUM at INR 11,067 Cr, up 13% YoY; Embedded Value of INR 2,333 Cr 
- Issued 15,591 policies in the quarter 
- Par and Non-Par products constituted 78% of new business premium in the quarter

governance. Edelweiss employs nearly 6,500 people, serves around 1.5 Cr customers, and manages around INR 2,90,000 Cr

considered and approved the following along with other items of business:

September 30, 2026 prepared under Indian Accounting Standards (IND-AS) and as per Regulation 33
of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)

information.

Declared second interim dividend of Rs. 1.25 (Rupees one rupee twenty five paise only)  ( 62.50%) each
per equity share of Rs.2/- (Rupees two only) each for the financial year 2026-27. The date for taking
on record of its shareholders eligible for the purpose of payment of second interim dividend i.e., record
date is fixed as Thursday, the 19th day of November 2026. The payment of said interim dividend will
start from November 27, 2026.
A Copy of Press release is also enclosed for your information.

Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call”
November 05, 2026
MANAGEMENT: MR. MARK SALDANHA – CHAIRMAN AND MANAGING 
DIRECTOR – MARKSANS PHARMA LIMITED
MR. JITENDRA SHARMA – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER 
– MARKSANS PHARMA LIMITED

Moderator:
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Marksans Pharma Q2 FY 2027 earnings 
conference call hosted by Systematix Institutional Equities Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please 
note that this conference is being recorded.
Now I hand the conference over to Mr. Vishal Manchanda from Systematix Institutional 
Equities Limited. Thank you. Over to you, Mr. Manchanda.
Vishal Manchanda:
Thanks, Siddhant. On behalf of Systematix Institutional Equities, I welcome you to the Q2 FY 
2027 earnings call of Marksans Pharma. We thank the Marksans Pharma management for 
giving us an opportunity to host the call. Today, we have with us the senior management of the 
company, represented by Mr. Mark Saldanha, Chairman and Managing Director, and Mr. 
Jitendra Sharma, Chief Financial Officer.
I will now hand over the call to the company management for opening remarks. Over to you, 
sir.
Mark Saldanha:
Thank you, Vishal. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining us for 
Marksans Pharma Q2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings conference call. We appreciate your continued 
interest in the company and your support. I am pleased to share that we have delivered our 
strongest quarterly performance. Q2 was a record quarter for us, with revenue from operations 
reaching INR940 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 30.5%.
More importantly, this growth was accompanied by strong improvement in profitability. 
EBITDA increased by 48.3% to INR214 crores, and our EBITDA margin expanded by 274 
basis points to 22.8%. What is particularly encouraging is the breadth and quality of this 
performance. Our growth is not dependent on a single geography or acquisition. We have seen 
strong momentum across Europe, U.K., and continue to grow in North America. The 
increasing traction in Australia and New Zealand helped us to achieve these numbers.
Even excluding the contribution from QliniQ, our underlying business delivered a growth of 
approximately 25%. At the same time, we maintained healthy profitability despite higher 
freight and input costs. This gives us confidence that the investments we made in our portfolio, 
commercial capabilities, and geographic expansions are translating into sustainable growth.
Our performance also demonstrates the strength of our geographically diversified business 
model. North America continues to provide us with a large and resilient base, while U.K., 
Europe, and Australia and New Zealand are emerging as increasingly meaningful growth 
engines. The diversification provides us with multiple avenues of growth and reduces our 
dependency on a single market.
Let me begin with U.K. and Europe. We have seen a particularly strong performance. Revenue 
from this region increased by 65% to approximately INR405 crores. As many of you can 
recall, FY 2026 was a relatively subdued year for our U.K. business.
Page 2 of 17

Marksans Pharma Limited
November 05, 2026
We used this period to work on fundamentals, strengthening our portfolio, preparing new 
product launches, and improving our market position. These efforts are now beginning to 
reflect in our performance. Even excluding the contribution from the acquisitions, our business 
in the region grew by 49% in Q2. Alongside the growth in our existing business, we are 
making progress on important strategic priorities: building our own commercial infrastructure 
in key European markets.
This will bring us closer to customers and give us better control over how we take our portfolio 
to the market. QliniQ in the Netherlands contributed approximately INR84 crores for the first 
half, while ABCnow and Marksans GmbH are strengthening our platform in Germany. These 
businesses are important building blocks of our European strategy, and over time, should 
increase the opportunity to introduce a wider portfolio and scale up our presence across the 
region.
Turning to North America, which remains our largest market and contributed 44.8% of the 
revenue, we recorded our highest ever quarterly revenue of INR421 crores, representing a 
growth of 8.7% year-on-year. This is an encouraging performance in the context of the 
economic environment in the U.S. market.
Our order book remains healthy and continues to build, giving us confidence that as we look 
ahead in the coming quarters, price erosion in our prescription products, although being in 
single digits, we are still looking extremely optimistic in the U.S. market. In Australia and 
New Zealand, revenue grew by 64% to approximately INR101 crores.
We are seeing good traction from the strategy we pursued to build a branded prescription 
business under Nova. Our Rx division is growing at a strong pace, and the growth we are now 
delivering in these markets is meaningfully ahead of the levels achieved in the previous year.
We are encouraged by this progress and remain positive about the opportunities ahead. Our 
Rest of World business remained impacted in the quarter by ongoing geopolitical disruptions 
in the Middle East and other regions, which affected the timing of certain shipments in the 
region. Importantly, this was largely an operational and timing-related impact rather than a 
change in underlying opportunities in these markets.
We continue to monitor the situation closely, and as conditions normalize, we expect shipment 
activities to recover progressively. As we look into the second half and beyond, our growth 
priorities remain clear. We will continue to deepen our presence in the existing markets, scale 
our newly established European platform, expand our product portfolio, and selectively enter 
markets where we see an attractive opportunity. Our healthy order book, expanding 
commercial capabilities, and strong financial position give us confidence in our ability to 
sustain profitable growth.
Importantly, we are pursuing these opportunities from a position of financial strength. Our 
strong cash generation and a net cash balance provide us the flexibility to continue to invest in 
our product pipeline and commercial capabilities while selectively evaluating acquisitions that 
Page 3 of 17

Marksans Pharma Limited
November 05, 2026
offer a compelling strategic and financial fit. We remain disciplined in capital allocation, 
focused on execution, and committed to creating sustainable long-term value.
With this, I hand over to Jitendra to take you through the financial performance.
Jitendra Sharma:
Thank you, sir, and good afternoon, everyone. I will take you through the financial 
performance for the second quarter, followed by the first half performance. Starting with Q2, 
total income stood at INR958 crores, registering year-on-year growth of 29.2%. Revenue from 
operations was INR940 crores, up 30.5% year-on-year and 11.8% sequentially.
Looking at the geographic mix, North America contributed INR421 crores, representing 44.8% 
of the revenue. U.K. and Europe contributed INR405 crores, or 43%. Australia and New 
Zealand contributed INR101 crores, or 10.7%, while the Rest of the World contributed INR14 
crores, or 1.5%. Gross profit increased year-on-year by 33.6% to INR550 crores, ahead of 
revenue growth. Gross margin improved by 135 basis points year-on-year to 58.5%. EBITDA 
increased year-on-year by 48.3%. Hello?
Moderator:
Hello. There was some sort of disturbance from the line of Mr. CFO. Just a moment. Mr. 
Jitendra?
Jitendra Sharma:
Yes.
Moderator:
Can you please continue?
Jitendra Sharma:
Yes, sure. Thank you. Gross profit increased year-on-year by 33.6% to INR550 crores, ahead 
of revenue growth. Gross margin improved by 135 basis points year-on-year to 58.5%. 
EBITDA increased year-on-year by 48.3% to INR214 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding 
by 274 basis points to 22.8%, ahead of our 20%-21% guidance range. During Q1, we benefited 
from consumption of lower-cost inventory.
However, we are now seeing an increase in inventory costs, resulting in gross margin moving 
to 58.5% from 59.1% in the previous quarter. Notably, freight costs have nearly doubled in the 
current environment. Higher freight contributed approximately INR20 crores to the sequential 
increase in other expenses. There has also been a slight increase in employee costs, of 
approximately INR8 crores, as we continue to strengthen our team and invest in the newer 
markets.
In addition, our German business incurred initial startup costs of a couple of crores as we 
prepare these operations for the next phase. Against this backdrop, delivering a record 
quarterly EBITDA and maintaining an EBITDA margin of 22.8% is particularly encouraging. 
It reflects the operating leverage in our business, an improving product and geography mix, 
and disciplined execution across our markets.
Profit before tax for the quarter was INR194 crores, up 45.1% year-on-year. Profit after tax 
increased by 44.8% to INR144 crores, with a net margin of 15%. Profit after tax declined 
sequentially to INR144 crores compared with INR159 crores in Q1, primarily due to higher 
depreciation and amortization following the commencement of amortization on acquisition-
Page 4 of 17

Marksans Pharma Limited
November 05, 2026
related intangible assets, lower other income as currency movements stabilized, and a higher 
effective tax rate of 25.8%.
Moving to the first half performance, total income stood at INR1,825 crores, up 33.4%, while 
revenue from operations increased by 32.9% to INR1,781 crores. Gross margin improved by 
137 basis points to 58.8%, supported in part by the lower average cost of inventory consumed, 
particularly during Q1. EBITDA grew by 74.7% to INR427 crores, with the margin expanding 
by 574 basis points to 24%. Profit after tax increased by 92.5% to INR303 crores, with a net 
margin of 16.6%.
The first half also benefited from the higher other income. Cash generation was another 
important highlight of the first half. Cash generated from operations was INR322 crores 
compared with INR75 crores in the corresponding period last year. Cash conversion, measured 
as operating cash flow as a percentage of EBITDA, improved to 75.2% from 30.7%.
After capital expenditure of INR46 crores, free cash flow stood at INR275 crores. We also 
continued to make progress in working capital management. The working capital cycle 
reduced to approximately 128 days in the first half of the year from 138 days in FY 2026. 
During H1, we deployed around INR95 crores towards acquisitions and paid a dividend of 
around INR41 crores.
Even after these outflows, our net cash position increased by INR135 crores during the period. 
As of September end, cash balance and current investments stood at INR1,124 crores. Our net 
cash position was therefore at INR1,095 crores, while net worth stood at INR3,367 crores. Our 
return ratios have also improved meaningfully. On a trailing 12-month basis, return on capital 
employed increased to 24.7% from 18.7%, while return on equity improved to 18.6% from 
13.6%. For H1, R&D expenditure was 2.6% of revenue.
To conclude, the first half reflected strong growth in revenue and profitability, healthy cash 
conversion, and continued improvement in capital efficiency. Thank you. We will now be 
happy to take your questions.

penetrate more volumes in the second half?
In general, how does the order book look? There were some comments on the consumer 
sentiment in U.S. How do you see the market and growth in the second half and in general for 
the U.S. business?
Mark Saldanha:
Obviously, seasonality being number one. A substantial amount of our portfolio is seasonal, 
which is obviously tilted more towards the cold season. The cold season has yet to. It normally 
Page 5 of 17

Marksans Pharma Limited
November 05, 2026
comes in October, November, December, is the season. That said and done, obviously, when 
we talk of sentiments, we talk about the geopolitical scenarios where we talk of inflation, crude 
oil, everything of that stuff, having impact on affordability in the U.S.
Obviously, with costs going up, I think medicines are literally the last priority on everyone's 
mind. Obviously, food and gas become the top priority for everyone else. All this coupled with 
seasonality, I mean, we have grown to some extent, and we will continue growing in the U.S. 
market. We are quite optimistic on achieving our objectives. We still believe within the next

Ahmed Madha:
The overall run rate is now close to almost INR1,000 crores, probably next quarter or so you

have a lot of cash available. Do we go into a major capex cycle next year or so?
Mark Saldanha:
Again, like I've said, our outlook is more long-term than immediate. We do believe we are 
trending and we are working and trending towards achieving INR5,000 crores in the next three 
years and possibly doubling our revenue from where we were last year within the next five 
years, INR6,000 odd crores. We are working towards that, and that would need, obviously, 
infusion of capex in terms of manufacturing infrastructure to support that growth phase.
Today, you're right, we are trending at INR1,000 crores a quarter, very close to INR1,000 
crores, but you can round it up to INR1,000 crores a quarter. That gives us some visibility on 
an INR4,000 crores mark. Today, we don't talk about INR4,000 crores. We are already

another plant. We are in active dialogue on both sides.
Ahmed Madha:
Okay, got it. Thank you so much.
Mark Saldanha:
Thank you.

Thank you. The next question comes from the line of Arun from Unifi Capital. Please go

Arun:
Sir, congratulations on your good set of numbers. Could you explain how revenue growth

conference call hosted by Systematix Institutional Equities Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference

note that this conference is being recorded.
Now I hand the conference over to Mr. Vishal Manchanda from Systematix Institutional 
Equities Limited. Thank you. Over to you, Mr. Manchanda.
Vishal Manchanda:
Thanks, Siddhant. On behalf of Systematix Institutional Equities, I welcome you to the Q2 FY 
2027 earnings call of Marksans Pharma. We thank the Marksans Pharma management for 
giving us an opportunity to host the call. Today, we have with us the senior management of the 
company, represented by Mr. Mark Saldanha, Chairman and Managing Director, and Mr. 
Jitendra Sharma, Chief Financial Officer.
I will now hand over the call to the company management for opening remarks. Over to you, 
sir.
Mark Saldanha:
Thank you, Vishal. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining us for 
Marksans Pharma Q2 and H1 FY 2027 earnings conference call. We appreciate your continued 
interest in the company and your support. I am pleased to share that we have delivered our 
strongest quarterly performance. Q2 was a record quarter for us, with revenue from operations 
reaching INR940 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 30.5%.
More importantly, this growth was accompanied by strong improvement in profitability. 
EBITDA increased by 48.3% to INR214 crores, and our EBITDA margin expanded by 274 
basis points to 22.8%. What is particularly encouraging is the breadth and quality of this 
performance. Our growth is not dependent on a single geography or acquisition. We have seen 
strong momentum across Europe, U.K., and continue to grow in North America. The 
increasing traction in Australia and New Zealand helped us to achieve these numbers.
Even excluding the contribution from QliniQ, our underlying business delivered a growth of 
approximately 25%. At the same time, we maintained healthy profitability despite higher 
freight and input costs. This gives us confidence that the investments we made in our portfolio, 
commercial capabilities, and geographic expansions are translating into sustainable growth.
Our performance also demonstrates the strength of our geographically diversified business 
model. North America continues to provide us with a large and resilient base, while U.K., 
Europe, and Australia and New Zealand are emerging as increasingly meaningful growth 
engines. The diversification provides us with multiple avenues of growth and reduces our 
dependency on a single market.
Let me begin with U.K. and Europe. We have seen a particularly strong performance. Revenue 
from this region increased by 65% to approximately INR405 crores. As many of you can 
recall, FY 2026 was a relatively subdued year for our U.K. business.
Page 2 of 17

Marksans Pharma Limited
November 05, 2026
We used this period to work on fundamentals, strengthening our portfolio, preparing new 
product launches, and improving our market position. These efforts are now beginning to 
reflect in our performance. Even excluding the contribution from the acquisitions, our business 
in the region grew by 49% in Q2. Alongside the growth in our existing business, we are 
making progress on important strategic priorities: building our own commercial infrastructure 
in key European markets.
This will bring us closer to customers and give us better control over how we take our portfolio 
to the market. QliniQ in the Netherlands contributed approximately INR84 crores for the first 
half, while ABCnow and Marksans GmbH are strengthening our platform in Germany. These 
businesses are important building blocks of our European strategy, and over time, should 
increase the opportunity to introduce a wider portfolio and scale up our presence across the 
region.
Turning to North America, which remains our largest market and contributed 44.8% of the 
revenue, we recorded our highest ever quarterly revenue of INR421 crores, representing a 
growth of 8.7% year-on-year. This is an encouraging performance in the context of the 
economic environment in the U.S. market.
Our order book remains healthy and continues to build, giving us confidence that as we look 
ahead in the coming quarters, price erosion in our prescription products, although being in 
single digits, we are still looking extremely optimistic in the U.S. market. In Australia and 
New Zealand, revenue grew by 64% to approximately INR101 crores.
We are seeing good traction from the strategy we pursued to build a branded prescription 
business under Nova. Our Rx division is growing at a strong pace, and the growth we are now 
delivering in these markets is meaningfully ahead of the levels achieved in the previous year.
We are encouraged by this progress and remain positive about the opportunities ahead. Our 
Rest of World business remained impacted in the quarter by ongoing geopolitical disruptions 
in the Middle East and other regions, which affected the timing of certain shipments in the 
region. Importantly, this was largely an operational and timing-related impact rather than a 
change in underlying opportunities in these markets.
We continue to monitor the situation closely, and as conditions normalize, we expect shipment 
activities to recover progressively. As we look into the second half and beyond, our growth 
priorities remain clear. We will continue to deepen our presence in the existing markets, scale 
our newly established European platform, expand our product portfolio, and selectively enter 
markets where we see an attractive opportunity. Our healthy order book, expanding 
commercial capabilities, and strong financial position give us confidence in our ability to 
sustain profitable growth.
Importantly, we are pursuing these opportunities from a position of financial strength. Our 
strong cash generation and a net cash balance provide us the flexibility to continue to invest in 
our product pipeline and commercial capabilities while selectively evaluating acquisitions that

offer a compelling strategic and financial fit. We remain disciplined in capital allocation, 
focused on execution, and committed to creating sustainable long-term value.

depreciation and amortization following the commencement of amortization on acquisition-

related intangible assets, lower other income as currency movements stabilized, and a higher 
effective tax rate of 25.8%.

Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Para A of Part A of Schedule Ill of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("Listing Regulations"), we wish to inform you that the 
Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on November 13, 2026, has approved the sale 
and transfer of the Distillery Unit of the Company situated at Udaikulam Village, Koothandan Post, 
Sivagangai District, Tamil Nadu, together with its employees, assets, licences, permits, insurance 
policies, contracts, interests, rights and liabilities ("Sivagangai Distillery Unit"), as a going concern by 
way of a slump sale pursuant to Section 2(103) and other applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act, 
2025, through a Business Transfer Agreement ("BTA"), subject to the fulfilment of the conditions 
precedent and such other terms and conditions as may be set out in the BTA. 
The details required under the Listing Regulations, read with SEBI Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-
CFD-POD2/l/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, are provided in Annexure A. 
This intimation is also being made available on the Company's website at www.eidparry.com. 
The meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company commenced at 10:00 a.m. and concluded at 
02:40 p.m. 
You are requested to kindly take the above on record. 
Thanking you, 
Yours faithfully, 
For E.I.D. - PARRY (INDIA) LIMITED 
Biswa Mohan Rath

The transaction is being undertaken as part of the 
Company's asset rationalisation strategy to optimise its 
asset portfolio and enable greater focus on its core

has faced challenges due to reduced availability of

economics associated with sourcing molasses from other

unlocking from the asset and enable more efficient 
deployment of the Company's resources towards its core 
and strategic businesses.

closure of operations of PSRIPL's sugar refinery unit with effect from the close of working hours on March 31. 2026. The subsidiary was engaged in the business of refining raw rugru: 
and exporting refined sugar. Over a sustained period, the operations were adversely impacted by changes in globaJ market conditions, higher operating costs. operational disruptions, 
etc. Despite various initiatives undertaken to improve operational perl'onnance and financial viability, the business continued to incur losses and was assessed to be unviable. 
Accordingly, after evaluating all strategic options, the Board of directors of PSRIPL concluded that closure of the operations was in the best long-term interest of the Company and its 
stakeholders. 
The Company had previously provided vanous guarantees and letters to the lenders of PSRIPL, Pursuant to the decision of the Board of Directors of the Company and PSRIPL d AICd 
March 3 1, 2026, discussions with the lenders and the disclosures made to the stock exchanges, the Company has reassessed and remeasured its financial guarantee obllga.tlon.s 
considering that PSRIPL 1s not expected 10 have adequate financial resources to settle its borrowings, after talcing into account the estimated realisable value of its assets. Accordingly, 
the Company has recognised a provismn towards financial guarantee obligations amounting to Rs. 59, 132 lakhs for the year-ended March 3 1, 2026, 
During the quarter ended June 30, 2026, pursuant to the Board's approval, the Company invested Rs. 6 1,000 lakhs in PSRJPL to meet the obligations of the subsidiary. Consequent ro 
the impairment of this investment in the quarter ended June 30. 2026 and the reversal of provisions made earlier of Rs. 59,132 lakhs, relating to financial guarantees that had be-en 
recognized as of March 31, 2026, a net additional impairment charge of Rs. 1,868 lakhs has been recognized during the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Rs. 35,444 lakhs ror the qunnc.r 
and six months ended September 30, 2025 and Rs. 40,060 lakhs for the year ended March 31, 2026). 
Further, the Company has committed to provide additional financial support to PSRIPL in the fonn of loans up to Rs. 13,000 lakhs to enable it to meet obligations arising from tho

closure of operations of PSRIPL's sugar refinery unit with effect from the close of working hours on March 31. 2026. The subsidiary was engaged in the business of refining raw rugru: 
and exporting refined sugar. Over a sustained period, the operations were adversely impacted by changes in globaJ market conditions, higher operating costs. operational disruptions, 
etc. Despite various initiatives undertaken to improve operational perl'onnance and financial viability, the business continued to incur losses and was assessed to be unviable. 
Accordingly, after evaluating all strategic options, the Board of directors of PSRIPL concluded that closure of the operations was in the best long-term interest of the Company and its 
stakeholders. 
The Company had previously provided vanous guarantees and letters to the lenders of PSRIPL, Pursuant to the decision of the Board of Directors of the Company and PSRIPL d AICd 
March 3 1, 2026, discussions with the lenders and the disclosures made to the stock exchanges, the Company has reassessed and remeasured its financial guarantee obllga.tlon.s 
considering that PSRIPL 1s not expected 10 have adequate financial resources to settle its borrowings, after talcing into account the estimated realisable value of its assets. Accordingly, 
the Company has recognised a provismn towards financial guarantee obligations amounting to Rs. 59, 132 lakhs for the year-ended March 3 1, 2026,

Subject: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on Interim Dividend 
 
We are pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors of Aptus Value Housing Finance India Limited 
(“Company”), at its Meeting held on November 04, 2026, has declared an interim dividend of Rs. 2/- 
(Indian Rupees Two only) per equity share of face value of Rs. 2/- for the financial year 2026-27. 
 
As you may be aware, in terms of the applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (“the Act”), 
dividend paid or distributed by a company is taxable in the hands of the shareholders. Accordingly, the 
Company is required to deduct tax at source at the time of credit of dividend to the account of the 
shareholder or at the time of payment, whichever is earlier. The applicable tax deduction / withholding 
rate may vary depending on the residential status and category of the shareholder. Accordingly, 
dividend will be paid after deduction of tax at source / withholding tax, including surcharge and cess, 
wherever applicable. 
 
All the shareholders are requested to update their records such as tax residential status, Permanent 
Account Number (PAN), bank account details and register your email address, mobile numbers and 
other details with your relevant depositories through your depository participants in case you are 
holding shares in dematerialized form and if you are holding shares in physical mode, you are requested 
to furnish details to the Company’s Registrar and Share Transfer Agent (“RTA”), i.e. KFin Technologies 
Limited1. 
This communication provides a brief of the applicable Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) provisions under 
the Act for Resident and Non-Resident shareholder categories.

Gillette India Ltd. Announces Second quarter results  
 
Driving consistent balanced growth - Sales up 4%, PAT up 11% for quarter ended September 30, 2026 
 
 
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: Gillette India Limited (GIL) today announced its financial results for the 
quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company delivered strong growth during the quarter, with sales 
of ₹846 crore, up 4% versus year ago. Profit After Tax (PAT) was reported at ₹159 crores, up 11% versus year 
ago. This balanced and broad-based growth was driven by the strength of its strategic portfolio, 
meaningful innovation that addresses evolving consumer needs, and superior retail execution across 
channels.  
 
Kumar Venkatasubramanian, Managing Director, Gillette India Ltd. said, “Our consistent delivery of 
balanced growth quarter on quarter is a true reflection of the strength of our integrated growth 
strategy, and the exceptional execution of these strategies by our people. This consistency is also 
reflected in our innovation – both in terms of our propositions as well as how we engage with consumers. 
We remain committed to our strategy to delight consumers with superior products at a superior value 
by putting the consumer first in everything we do.” 
 
He added, “Our integrated growth strategy is anchored in a focused portfolio, superiority (of product 
performance, packaging, brand communication, retail execution and value), productivity, constructive 
disruption and an empowered, agile organization.” 
 
For the quarter, profitability was impacted by significant commodity headwinds. However, the Company 
has been able to leverage its robust productivity program to mitigate the headwinds and deliver 
profitable growth.  
 
The company’s power Oral Care business delivered strong results, growing double digit, driven by 
superior execution of strategies and the launch of Oral B iO2 - built for the easiest switch from manual to 
power oral care, enabling consumers to pick one of Oral-B’s most impactful oral health tools that provides 
perfect clean even on the last tooth. 
 
The first half of FY 2026–27 has been defined by bold innovation across the vectors of superiority. This 
momentum was anchored by key product introductions – including the launch of Gillette Guard 3in1 and 
Gillette AIO Trimmer series – and an evolving media model designed to reach consumers where they are. 
Recently, the company also participated in P&G Loop, a first-of-its-kind, mega immersive brand 
experience event organized for content creators.  
 
 
About Gillette India Ltd.: 
Gillette India Limited (GIL) is one of India’s well-known FMCG Companies that has some of the world’s 
leading brands Gillette and Oral B; and has carved a reputation for delivering superior products to meet 
the needs of consumers. GIL brands take pride in being socially conscious via their participation in P&G 
Shiksha, P&G India’s flagship CSR program that supports the education of underprivileged children in 
India.  Please visit in.pg.com for the latest news.  
 
For details contact: Madison Public Relations:  
Malika Bhavnani +91 9820496099; malika.bhavnani@madisonpr.in

profitable growth.

superior execution of strategies and the launch of Oral B iO2 - built for the easiest switch from manual to 
power oral care, enabling consumers to pick one of Oral-B’s most impactful oral health tools that provides 
perfect clean even on the last tooth. 
 
The first half of FY 2026–27 has been defined by bold innovation across the vectors of superiority. This 
momentum was anchored by key product introductions – including the launch of Gillette Guard 3in1 and 
Gillette AIO Trimmer series – and an evolving media model designed to reach consumers where they are. 
Recently, the company also participated in P&G Loop, a first-of-its-kind, mega immersive brand 
experience event organized for content creators.  
 
 
About Gillette India Ltd.: 
Gillette India Limited (GIL) is one of India’s well-known FMCG Companies that has some of the world’s 
leading brands Gillette and Oral B; and has carved a reputation for delivering superior products to meet

9,144
Ramp-up to full capacity is gated by the pace of Indian Railways tender issuance, not by capability. Structural demand drivers remain strong:
Freight loading target
Indian Railways currently loads ~1.6 billion tonnes, targeted 
to reach 3 billion tonnes by FY2030.
Infrastructure already funded
Over ₹20 lakh crore invested in the last 10 years — dedicated 
freight corridors, new Siemens locomotive contract and 
more.
Modal share push
To service that capex, rail must lift its freight market share 
from ~25% today to a target of 40%.
Gati Shakti logistics cost
National logistics cost of ~14% is targeted down to 9%, 
achievable only by shifting movement to rail.
Policy impetus to wagons
New policy allows special-purpose wagon design and 
ownership, bringing non-conventional commodities onto rail; 
leasing and private ownership of wagons and freight terminals 
encouraged.
National Rail Plan gap
Wagon fleet to go from 3 lakh in FY2022 to 6 lakh by FY2030. 
Only ~1 lakh purchased so far — a delta of 2 lakh wagons.

31
•
Setting up Brownfield Shipyard at Falta with a total project cost of ~ Rs 
610 crores
•
TNSL received in-principle approval under the Shipbuilding Development 
Scheme for capital assistance of ~ Rs 129 crores towards plant and 
machinery for the brownfield expansion of its Falta Shipyard.
•
Advanced discussions underway for a major export order with an 
overseas client, supported by strategic engagement with a leading global 
design house for access to proven vessel designs.
•
Exploring technology partnerships and potential joint ventures with 
shipyards to expand opportunities in small vessels, passenger ferries, 
and craft.
•
Working with leading international partners for the development and 
construction of hovercraft for the Indian Coast Guard.
•
Applying for being Upgraded from Category-D to Category-C shipyard 
status for upcoming Indian Navy opportunities, including FIC, FAC, and 
NGMV.
•
Establishing an integrated platform for 60T BP E-Tugs with standardized 
designs, streamlined assembly, and Robust supply-chain partnerships.
•
Modernizing capabilities for small craft and vessels up to 120 m, targeting 
opportunities with ONGC, IWAI, Indian Navy, Coast Guard, and 
Sagarmala
•
Expected support from the Government of West Bengal and the Centre 
for strategic development initiatives at the Falta Shipyard.

Update on Rail Wheel Project (JV with RKFL)
33
•
Titagarh Rail Systems & Ramkrishna Forgings  Consortium received an 
LOA for Manufacturing and Supplying of Forged Wheels for the Indian 
Railways.
•
The Company holds 49 % stake in the Joint Venture. 
•
The JV will establish Asia’s 2nd largest manufacturing plant in India to 
produce 228,000 forged wheels per annum. 
•
The total project cost is estimated at ~₹2,181 crores across two 
phases, which is being funded through a mix of debt and equity.
•
A total of ₹532.65 crores equity has been infused in the JV by both 
parties (as on September 30, 2026)
•
Plant at Chennai, Tamil Nadu; trial production has started and the 
commercial production will commence shortly.
•
300 trial wheels produced and under inspection by Indian Railways; 
approval expected shortly.
•
Partial production from November / December 2026 at 2,000–3,000 
wheels/month, ramping to 4,000–5,000 in Q4 FY27; ~20,000–25,000 
wheels expected to be supplied in FY27.

34

Titagarh Rail Systems Limited ("TRSL") and Bharat Heavy Electricals 
Limited ("BHEL") signed the Joint Venture Agreement on September 15, 
2026, to incorporate a new private limited company in New Delhi, with 
initial paid-up capital of ₹50 lakh, for comprehensive maintenance of 
the Vande Bharat Sleeper Trainsets.

O/S ORDER BOOK
9,144
Ramp-up to full capacity is gated by the pace of Indian Railways tender issuance, not by capability. Structural demand drivers remain strong:
Freight loading target
Indian Railways currently loads ~1.6 billion tonnes, targeted 
to reach 3 billion tonnes by FY2030.
Infrastructure already funded
Over ₹20 lakh crore invested in the last 10 years — dedicated 
freight corridors, new Siemens locomotive contract and 
more.
Modal share push
To service that capex, rail must lift its freight market share 
from ~25% today to a target of 40%.
Gati Shakti logistics cost
National logistics cost of ~14% is targeted down to 9%, 
achievable only by shifting movement to rail.
Policy impetus to wagons
New policy allows special-purpose wagon design and 
ownership, bringing non-conventional commodities onto rail; 
leasing and private ownership of wagons and freight terminals 
encouraged.
National Rail Plan gap
Wagon fleet to go from 3 lakh in FY2022 to 6 lakh by FY2030. 
Only ~1 lakh purchased so far — a delta of 2 lakh wagons.

Ramp-up to full capacity is gated by the pace of Indian Railways tender issuance, not by capability. Structural demand drivers remain strong:
Freight loading target
Indian Railways currently loads ~1.6 billion tonnes, targeted 
to reach 3 billion tonnes by FY2030.
Infrastructure already funded
Over ₹20 lakh crore invested in the last 10 years — dedicated 
freight corridors, new Siemens locomotive contract and 
more.
Modal share push
To service that capex, rail must lift its freight market share 
from ~25% today to a target of 40%.
Gati Shakti logistics cost
National logistics cost of ~14% is targeted down to 9%, 
achievable only by shifting movement to rail.
Policy impetus to wagons
New policy allows special-purpose wagon design and 
ownership, bringing non-conventional commodities onto rail; 
leasing and private ownership of wagons and freight terminals 
encouraged.
National Rail Plan gap
Wagon fleet to go from 3 lakh in FY2022 to 6 lakh by FY2030. 
Only ~1 lakh purchased so far — a delta of 2 lakh wagons.

Ramp-up to full capacity is gated by the pace of Indian Railways tender issuance, not by capability. Structural demand drivers remain strong:
Freight loading target
Indian Railways currently loads ~1.6 billion tonnes, targeted 
to reach 3 billion tonnes by FY2030.
Infrastructure already funded
Over ₹20 lakh crore invested in the last 10 years — dedicated 
freight corridors, new Siemens locomotive contract and 
more.
Modal share push
To service that capex, rail must lift its freight market share 
from ~25% today to a target of 40%.
Gati Shakti logistics cost
National logistics cost of ~14% is targeted down to 9%, 
achievable only by shifting movement to rail.
Policy impetus to wagons
New policy allows special-purpose wagon design and 
ownership, bringing non-conventional commodities onto rail; 
leasing and private ownership of wagons and freight terminals 
encouraged.
National Rail Plan gap
Wagon fleet to go from 3 lakh in FY2022 to 6 lakh by FY2030. 
Only ~1 lakh purchased so far — a delta of 2 lakh wagons.

Blackbox Delivers Second Consecutive Quarter of Record-Breaking Financial Performance 
Order Backlog of US$1.04 billion, up 88% YOY | Revenue of ₹1,936 crore in Q2 FY27, up 22% YOY 
EBITDA of ₹175 crore in Q2 FY27, up 23% YOY | PAT of ₹73 crore in Q2 FY27, up 31% YOY 
 
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: Black Box Limited (BSE: 500463 | NSE: BBOX), a global digital 
infrastructure solutions provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half 
year ended September 30, 2026.  
Black Box reported record quarterly revenue of ₹1,936 crore, up 22% year-on-year and 13% 
sequentially. EBITDA increased 23% YOY to ₹175 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 31% to            
₹73 crore.  
Growth was driven by continued execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise 
solutions, supported by growing momentum in the Company's Technology Products business.  
The Company's order backlog reached a record US$1,044 million, up 88% YoY, strengthening visibility 
for continued growth.

Sanjeev Verma, Whole-time Director & Chief Executive Officer, Black Box Limited said, “Black 
Box is building strong growth momentum, with record quarterly revenue and an order backlog exceeding 
US$1 billion. These results reinforce our confidence in scaling the business towards our immediate 
growth goal of US$2 billion in revenue. 
 
Our data centre business is a powerful growth engine, with significant orders from multiple hyperscalers 
and repeat wins expanding our role in their infrastructure investments. Our strong U.S. presence, deep 
expertise and proven execution position us to capture a greater share of accelerating data centre 
investment, supported by a substantial opportunity pipeline. Growing Enterprise and Technology 
Products businesses across the United States and international markets further strengthen our growth 
outlook. 
 
With secured orders and proven delivery capabilities, we are ready to execute at greater scale. 
Continued hiring, investment in our people and expansion of delivery capacity strengthen our ability to 
deliver larger projects and drive our next phase of growth.”  
 
Deepak Kumar Bansal, Executive Director & Global CFO, Black Box Limited  
“Our Q2 performance demonstrates the growing earnings strength of Black Box, with PAT rising 31% 
to ₹73 crore, ahead of revenue growth of 22%. H1 EBITDA margin expanded 50 basis points to 9.2%, 

 
2 
 
while operating cash flow reached ₹115 crore for the first half of FY27. We are translating growth into 
stronger profitability and cash generation. 
 
Our expanding data centre business and significant order pipeline provide a strong foundation to scale 
revenue and earnings. As secured orders convert into revenue, we see further opportunities to improve 
operating leverage and build on this earnings momentum. 
  
We are confident of achieving our FY27 guidance of 23–27% revenue growth and 38–50% PAT growth, 
with profit growth expected to remain in high double digits for the next few years along with stronger 
cash flow generation. Disciplined working capital management and prudent capital allocation remain 
central to converting this opportunity into sustained shareholder value.”  
 
Hyperscale Infrastructure: Capturing AI-Driven Investment Opportunities  
Accelerating investment in AI infrastructure is driving demand for hyperscale data centre capacity, 
connectivity and network infrastructure. Black Box is expanding its participation in this market through 
established hyperscaler relationships, technical expertise and large-scale project delivery capabilities. 
  
Black Box secured over US$250 million in data centre orders in H1 FY27. A substantial pipeline of large 
hyperscale deals is expected to drive significant order wins and accelerate growth in the coming 
quarters. 
  
Black Box supports infrastructure projects associated with large-scale data centre developments with 
gigawatt-scale capacity. Its experience in delivering complex projects provides opportunities to expand 
existing customer relationships and participate in larger infrastructure projects. 
  
The Company continues to strengthen its engineering and delivery capabilities, particularly in the United 
States, to support this demand.  
 
Record Backlog Strengthens Revenue Visibility  
Black Box secured US$298 million in new orders during Q2 FY27, up 37% YOY. The order backlog 
reached a record US$1,044 million, increasing 88% YOY and approximately 10% sequentially. The 
backlog includes a growing proportion of larger, multi-year engagements, with project-led wins providing 
revenue visibility over 24 to 36 months. 
  
Supported by its order pipeline across hyperscale, enterprise and presence across multiple countries, 
Black Box management is confident to achieve its FY27 guidance of: 
  
• 
Exit order backlog: US$1.3–1.4 billion   
• 
Order bookings: US$1.3–1.5 billion  
• 
Revenue growth: 23–27%  
• 
EBITDA growth: 27-32% 
• 
PAT growth: 38–50%  
 
Enterprise and Technology Products: Expanding Growth Opportunities  
Black Box continues to deepen its enterprise relationships across the United States and international 
markets, supporting customers across technology, healthcare, financial services, industrial and retail 
markets.  
  
During Q2 FY27, the Company secured engagements involving network infrastructure, connectivity, 
data centre integration and digital workplace solutions. Key wins included projects with a leading Indian 
telecom operator, global technology and semiconductor companies, US healthcare providers, a global 
pharmaceutical company, a major US financial institution, and retail and public sector customers. These 

 
3 
 
engagements reinforce the Company's diversified customer base and its strategy of expanding 
relationships with 300 strategic enterprise accounts. 
  
The Technology Products business is gaining momentum as customers modernise critical operations 
and invest in secure, resilient control room platforms. This creates further opportunities for Black Box’s 
specialised technology portfolio. 
  
Together, Enterprise Solutions and Technology Products businesses provide complementary growth 
opportunities alongside the expanding hyperscale data center business.  
 
Investing in Capabilities for Sustainable Growth

Blackbox Delivers Second Consecutive Quarter of Record-Breaking Financial Performance 
Order Backlog of US$1.04 billion, up 88% YOY | Revenue of ₹1,936 crore in Q2 FY27, up 22% YOY 
EBITDA of ₹175 crore in Q2 FY27, up 23% YOY | PAT of ₹73 crore in Q2 FY27, up 31% YOY 
 
Mumbai, November 13, 2026: Black Box Limited (BSE: 500463 | NSE: BBOX), a global digital 
infrastructure solutions provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half 
year ended September 30, 2026.  
Black Box reported record quarterly revenue of ₹1,936 crore, up 22% year-on-year and 13% 
sequentially. EBITDA increased 23% YOY to ₹175 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 31% to            
₹73 crore.  
Growth was driven by continued execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise 
solutions, supported by growing momentum in the Company's Technology Products business.  
The Company's order backlog reached a record US$1,044 million, up 88% YoY, strengthening visibility 
for continued growth.

Sanjeev Verma, Whole-time Director & Chief Executive Officer, Black Box Limited said, “Black 
Box is building strong growth momentum, with record quarterly revenue and an order backlog exceeding 
US$1 billion. These results reinforce our confidence in scaling the business towards our immediate 
growth goal of US$2 billion in revenue. 
 
Our data centre business is a powerful growth engine, with significant orders from multiple hyperscalers 
and repeat wins expanding our role in their infrastructure investments. Our strong U.S. presence, deep 
expertise and proven execution position us to capture a greater share of accelerating data centre 
investment, supported by a substantial opportunity pipeline. Growing Enterprise and Technology 
Products businesses across the United States and international markets further strengthen our growth 
outlook. 
 
With secured orders and proven delivery capabilities, we are ready to execute at greater scale. 
Continued hiring, investment in our people and expansion of delivery capacity strengthen our ability to 
deliver larger projects and drive our next phase of growth.”  
 
Deepak Kumar Bansal, Executive Director & Global CFO, Black Box Limited  
“Our Q2 performance demonstrates the growing earnings strength of Black Box, with PAT rising 31% 
to ₹73 crore, ahead of revenue growth of 22%. H1 EBITDA margin expanded 50 basis points to 9.2%, 

 
2 
 
while operating cash flow reached ₹115 crore for the first half of FY27. We are translating growth into 
stronger profitability and cash generation. 
 
Our expanding data centre business and significant order pipeline provide a strong foundation to scale 
revenue and earnings. As secured orders convert into revenue, we see further opportunities to improve 
operating leverage and build on this earnings momentum. 
  
We are confident of achieving our FY27 guidance of 23–27% revenue growth and 38–50% PAT growth, 
with profit growth expected to remain in high double digits for the next few years along with stronger 
cash flow generation. Disciplined working capital management and prudent capital allocation remain 
central to converting this opportunity into sustained shareholder value.”  
 
Hyperscale Infrastructure: Capturing AI-Driven Investment Opportunities  
Accelerating investment in AI infrastructure is driving demand for hyperscale data centre capacity, 
connectivity and network infrastructure. Black Box is expanding its participation in this market through 
established hyperscaler relationships, technical expertise and large-scale project delivery capabilities. 
  
Black Box secured over US$250 million in data centre orders in H1 FY27. A substantial pipeline of large 
hyperscale deals is expected to drive significant order wins and accelerate growth in the coming 
quarters. 
  
Black Box supports infrastructure projects associated with large-scale data centre developments with 
gigawatt-scale capacity. Its experience in delivering complex projects provides opportunities to expand 
existing customer relationships and participate in larger infrastructure projects. 
  
The Company continues to strengthen its engineering and delivery capabilities, particularly in the United 
States, to support this demand.  
 
Record Backlog Strengthens Revenue Visibility  
Black Box secured US$298 million in new orders during Q2 FY27, up 37% YOY. The order backlog 
reached a record US$1,044 million, increasing 88% YOY and approximately 10% sequentially. The 
backlog includes a growing proportion of larger, multi-year engagements, with project-led wins providing 
revenue visibility over 24 to 36 months. 
  
Supported by its order pipeline across hyperscale, enterprise and presence across multiple countries, 
Black Box management is confident to achieve its FY27 guidance of: 
  
• 
Exit order backlog: US$1.3–1.4 billion   
• 
Order bookings: US$1.3–1.5 billion  
• 
Revenue growth: 23–27%  
• 
EBITDA growth: 27-32% 
• 
PAT growth: 38–50%  
 
Enterprise and Technology Products: Expanding Growth Opportunities  
Black Box continues to deepen its enterprise relationships across the United States and international 
markets, supporting customers across technology, healthcare, financial services, industrial and retail 
markets.  
  
During Q2 FY27, the Company secured engagements involving network infrastructure, connectivity, 
data centre integration and digital workplace solutions. Key wins included projects with a leading Indian 
telecom operator, global technology and semiconductor companies, US healthcare providers, a global 
pharmaceutical company, a major US financial institution, and retail and public sector customers. These 

 
3 
 
engagements reinforce the Company's diversified customer base and its strategy of expanding 
relationships with 300 strategic enterprise accounts. 
  
The Technology Products business is gaining momentum as customers modernise critical operations 
and invest in secure, resilient control room platforms. This creates further opportunities for Black Box’s 
specialised technology portfolio. 
  
Together, Enterprise Solutions and Technology Products businesses provide complementary growth 
opportunities alongside the expanding hyperscale data center business.  
 
Investing in Capabilities for Sustainable Growth  
Black Box continues to strengthen its leadership, engineering, sales and delivery capabilities to support 
larger and more complex customer projects. The Company is progressing with its plan to recruit nearly 
3,000 professionals by FY30, primarily in the United States, with hiring already underway for major data 
centre projects. These investments support the Company's ambition of reaching US$2 billion in annual 
revenue by FY30, driven by expanding customer relationships, broader capabilities and disciplined 
execution.
