Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Happy Forgings Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call. Before we begin, a brief disclaimer. This conference call may contain forward-
looking statements about the company, which are based on the beliefs, opinions, and 
expectations of the company as on date of this call. These statements are not the guarantee of 
future performance of the company, and it may involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult 
to predict. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode. There will be an opportunity 
for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need any assistance during 
this conference, please signal for an operator by pressing star followed by zero on your touch-
tone telephones. Please note that this conference call is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ashish Garg, Managing Director from Happy Forgings 
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Ashish Garg: 
Good morning, and a very warm welcome to all of you to Happy Forgings Limited Q2 FY27 
earnings call. With me, I have Mr. Pankaj Kumar Goyal, our CFO, and Strategic Growth 
Advisors, our Investor Relations Advisors. I trust everyone had the chance to review our 
financial statements and the investor presentation for quarter two FY27, which we have filed 
with the exchanges. 
 
Let me start by outlining the key highlights for Q2 and H1 FY27. At the beginning of the year, 
we were optimistic about the business outlook for FY27, supported by improving demand 
conditions across our key end-user segments and good visibility on incremental business 
opportunities. I am pleased that we have delivered a strong performance during the first half of 
FY27, sustaining strong growth while maintaining the quality of our earnings. 
We have been able to sustain profitability levels at or above those achieved in FY2026, despite 
an increase in raw material prices and other cost pressures. This has enabled us to deliver 
profitability growth ahead of revenue growth, reflecting the strength of our diversified business 
portfolio, increasing value addition, and our continued focus on operational excellence. 
For H1 FY27, revenue grew by around 30% year-on-year, supported by a 24% increase in 
finished goods volume, reflecting a positive demand momentum across our key end markets, 
and realizations grew by around 5% to Rs.260 per kg. 
This growth has translated into improved profitability, with margins remaining healthy and 
return ratios showing an improvement. ROE increased to 17.1% and ROCE to 19.6%, reflecting 

 
Happy Forging Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 20 
 
better operational leverage, increasing value addition, and more efficient utilization of our 
capital. 
Growth was also broad-based across geographies, with domestic and export revenues increased 
by 30% and 36% respectively. Overall, the first half performance reflects our ability to deliver 
strong growth while maintaining a healthy balance between volumes and profitability. 
Moving to our quarterly performance, Q2FY27 was another strong quarter for the company. Our 
quarterly revenue crossed Rs.500 crores milestone, registering year-on-year growth of 
approximately 33%. Finished goods volume sales increased by around 25%, where realizations 
improved by roughly 6% to Rs.267 per kg. 
The improvement in realizations was supported by raw material cost pass-throughs, negotiated 
price increases to recover higher conversion costs, and a favorable product mix. Despite certain 
cost-related headwinds, our gross, EBITDA, and PAT margins remained healthy and broadly 
stable year on year, with only a margin moderation sequentially. 
This performance reinforces the resilience of our business model and our ability to sustain 
growth while maintaining profitability. Now moving to the segmental performance. Commercial 
vehicle continued to be our largest business segment, contributing 33% of our total revenue in 
H1 FY2027, compared to 37% in H1 FY2026. 
The segment registered high-teen growth during the period, primarily driven by a strong 
domestic performance, which grew in the mid-20s, broadly in line with the growth in the MHCV 
production and sales in India. Demand was supported by sustained infrastructure development, 
healthy replacement demand, and continued transportation activity. 
Exports, however, remained subdued, largely due to longer shipment times and resulting in 
higher sales in transit. Farm equipment was our second-largest segment, contributing 30% of 
our total revenues during H1 FY2027, compared to 34% in the corresponding period last year. 
The segment delivered growth of over 20%, with the domestic business registered high-teen 
growth, outperforming the growth in the domestic tractor production and sales during the period. 
Our export business also recorded a robust growth, supported by higher sales to some of our key 
customers, despite a challenging demand environment in key international markets. 
The industrial segment contributed 16% to our revenue, compared to 13% in H1 FY2026, 
registering a growth well above 50%. Growth was supported by strong traction in both domestic 
and export markets. Looking ahead, our investments in heavy forging capabilities, combined 
with growing demand for backup power generators for data centers in the energy sector, provide 
a strong basis for continued growth in this segment. 
Off-highway contributed 12% to our total revenue in H1 FY2027, compared to 10% in H1 
FY2026, registering a growth of over 50%, with both domestic and export markets contributing 
to this performance. 

 
Happy Forging Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 20 
 
The domestic construction equipment segment witnessed healthy growth during the quarter, 
supported by healthy project awards, particularly across road, highways, and infrastructure 
segments. On the export front, demand was supported by continued traction in construction and 
mining equipment markets. 
Passenger vehicle contribution has now increased to 9% of our total revenues in H1 FY2027 
compared to 5% in H1 FY2026. This segment revenue almost doubled over the corresponding 
period last year, with contribution coming from both domestic and export markets. Domestic 
revenues growth was supported by a healthy market demand and an increased wallet share, while 
export revenues growth was supported by execution of export orders secured in earlier periods. 
We continue to focus on improving the quality of our product mix with an increasing emphasis 
on higher value-added machining operations. Our machining contribution increased to 90% in 
H1 FY2027 compared to 88% in H1 FY2026. 
On the capacity front, our installed capacity forging capacity stands at 1,58,000 metric tons, 
while our machining capacity stands at 82,000 metric tons. During H1 FY2027, capacity 
utilization stood at 60% in forging and 77% in machining. We also strengthened our 
manufacturing capabilities during the period, commissioning a new forging press in Q1 FY2027 
and an additional hammer in Q2 FY2027. 
Our strategic investments are progressing as planned. The Rs.650 crores capex on ultra-heavy 
component manufacturing is going as per the scheduled timelines. This facility, with our 20 MW 
captive solar power plant, is expected to be completed and commence operation in the quarter 
four of FY2028. 
In parallel, we are actively engaged with several OEMs for heavy components catering to data 
center and gas engine application, as well as the wind program, which are continually in 
discussion. 
These discussions are progressing well, and we expect them to translate into orders in early 
FY2028. Further considering the strong demand visibility, healthy order books, and existing 
capacity utilizations now nearing their peak, our board has approved an additional capex of 
Rs.500 crores. 
This investment will be funded through a combination of debt and internal accruals and will be 
implemented in a phased manner across FY2028 and FY2029. The proposed investment will 
primarily focus on our expanding machining capabilities while supplementing our existing 
forging capabilities and will be best suited to growing requirements of our customers. 
These investments will mainly support growth opportunities across passenger vehicle, 
industrials, and export-related commercial vehicle sector. Combined together, the investment is 
in heavy components and newly approved capex. 
These plans involve an additional 59,000 metric tons of forging capacity and 34,000 tons of 
machining capacity, leading to a total capacity of around 2,17,000 tons in forging and 1,16,000 
tons in machining in next two to two and a half years. 

 
Happy Forging Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 20 
 
We believe that the planned capacity additions along our ongoing strategic investments will 
further strengthen our manufacturing capabilities and position us to capitalize on emerging 
opportunities and supporting our long-term growth ambitions. 
Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the demand environment and our growth prospects. 
Improving industry demand and the ramp-up of recently secured business provide confidence in 
our volume growth trajectory. Supported by our healthy order book, we remain well-positioned 
to meet our full-year volume growth guidance. 
While higher raw material prices and increased shipment cost may exert some near-term pressure 
on margins, we expect that our gross margin and EBITDA per kg metrics will continue to trend 
upwards, supported by a favorable product mix, higher value addition, and continued operational 
efficiencies. Full-year profitability margin metrics may remain at levels roughly similar to 
FY2026. 
With that, I would like to invite Mr. Pankaj Kumar Goyal, our CFO, to take you through the 
detailed financial performance of the quarter.

operational highlights for Q2 and H1 FY2027. First on revenue. Revenue from operation stood 
at Rs.501 crores for Q2 FY2027 and at Rs.950 crores for H1 FY2027, registering a strong year-
on-year growth of 32.7% and 29.9% respectively. 
 
I am pleased to share that our revenue performance for the period reflects both strong operational 
momentum and the strategic execution of our diversification strategy across key industry 
verticals and customer accounts. 
 
Looking at the number, our Q2 revenue growth was backed by strong dual engines, a 24.8% 
expansion in volumes and 6.3% increase in realizations. For the first half overall, this momentum 
carried through, with H1 volumes growing by 24% and realizations expanding by 4.8%. 
Our revenue growth is increasingly supported by broader industry diversification and lower 
customer concentration, with a growing contribution from customers beyond our top 10 
customers. 
Turning to profitability and margins. For Q2 FY2027, gross profit reached Rs.305 crores, 
delivering a robust year-on-year growth of 33.8%, with gross margin expanding 52 basis points 
to 60.8%. EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.153 crores, up 32.2% year-on-year, maintaining 
healthy and stable EBITDA margins at 30.6%. 
Our PAT came in at Rs.98 crores, marking an impressive 32.8% year-on-year growth, with PAT 
margin holding steady at 19.5%. On a cumulative basis for H1 FY2027, our performance was 
equally compelling. Gross profit grew 33.5% year-on-year to Rs.577 crores, with gross margin 
expanding by 161 basis points to 60.8%. EBITDA rose 35.5% year-on-year to Rs.294 crores, 
expanding EBITDA margin by 127 basis points to 30.9%.

Finally, PAT for the first half expanded 35.8% year-on-year to Rs.189 crores, with PAT margin 
broadening by 86 basis points to 19.9%. Overall, these numbers demonstrate both operating 
leverage and disciplined cost management as we scaled. 
Moving on to our balance sheet, cash flows, and capital allocation. Our financial position 
remains exceptionally strong, providing us with immense flexibility to fund ongoing growth. 
During H1 FY2027, we incurred a total expenditure of approximately Rs.378 crores, funded 
prudently through a combination of internal accruals, available liquidity, and targeted debts. 
Notably, over the last two and a half years, we have almost doubled our gross block, and this

cash flow for H1 stood at around Rs.124 crores. 
This temporary impact was primarily driven by working capital investment, especially higher 
receivables aligned with the high top-line expansions, alongside Rs.35 crores in strategic 
advance payments to raw material suppliers. We expect working capital movements to 
normalize over the full year, yielding significantly stronger cash flow conversion. 
Crucially, our balance sheet leverage remains extremely low. Our total outside liability to total 
net worth ratio stands at just 0.21x, leaving ample headroom to support working capital 
requirements via internal accruals or low-cost lines. 
Overall balance sheet health metrics remain best in class. Net debt to equity stands at a 
conservative 0.08x. ROCE came in at 19.6%, while ROCE on operational assets, excluding cash,

Moderator 
Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I am Kartikeyan, moderator for this conference. Welcome to the 
conference call of RITES Limited to discuss its Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27 results. We have with us today, Mr. 
Rahul Mithal, Chairman and Managing Director; Dr.Deepak Tripathi, Director (Technical); Mr. Krishna 
Gopal Agarwal, Director of Finance and Chief Financial Officer; and Mr. Prem Singh Meena, Director 
(Projects).  
At this moment, all participants are in listen-only mode. Later, we will conduct a question-and-answer 
session. At that time, if you have a question, please press * and 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note 
this conference is being recorded, and in the interest of time and fairness to all participants, you are 
requested to restrict yourself to one question per participant. If time permits, you may come back in the 
question queue.  
Now, I would like to hand over the floor to Mr. Rahul Mithal, Chairman and Managing Director, RITES 
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
 
Rahul Mithal 
Good morning, everyone. Let me start with giving the safe harbor statement. The presentation and the 
press release, which we uploaded on our website and exchanges yesterday and discussions during the call 
today may have some forward-looking statements. These statements consider the environment we see 
as of today and obviously carry a risk in terms of uncertainty because of which the actual results could be 
different, and we do not undertake to update those statements periodically.  
At the outset, I would like to just correct Kartikeyan, Director (Projects), Mr. Meena, has not been able to 
join due to some exigency. The other directors are here and the company secretary.  
Let me give the opening summary on our perception of the Q2 results. The performance has been muted, 
and an analysis of it shows that it is primarily due to two to three important revenue milestones sliding 
marginally by a few days (10-15 days) into Q3. So that has affected both the top line and the bottom line, 
then that has had an impact both on YoY, both Q2 as well as H1 to H1. 
But the way the execution has been planned, we are quite reassured and confident that the guidance 
which we had given at the beginning of the FY and reiterated at the end of Q1, that remains on track. So, 
that's the broad overview, and I'll get into details as we proceed ahead with the detailed questions. 
 
Moderator 
Thank you, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, now, we begin the question-and-answer session. If you have a 
question, please press * and 1 on your telephone keypad. In the interest of time and fairness to all 
participants, you are requested to restrict yourself to one question per participant. Time permits, you may

The first question is from the line of Gaurav Giridhar, an individual investor. Please go ahead. 
 
Gaurav Giridhar 
Good morning, sir. Thank you for giving me the opportunity. I'd just like to ask that how would be the 
margins going forward? Will they be, you know, on a growth trajectory? Will they be on the same level? 
How would it be? 
 
Rahul Mithal 
Morning, Gaurav. So, if you see the margins for Q2 and also if you see the margins on an H1, we are the 
EBITDA margins on a console basis are at 22% and 17% on the PAT margin, which as we have been giving 
the red lines for EBITDA margin on 18-20% and PAT margins for about 15-16%. These red lines, we are 
very confident that even on a quarterly basis, on a half-yearly basis, and an annual basis, we will not 
breach in any way.  
However, on a particular quarter, based on the blend, because as you see, in this quarter itself, there has 
been a substantial contribution of the turnkey segment. YoY, there's an increase in about INR 70 crores in 
turnkey, whereas export, there's a dip of INR 60 crores. There was zero booking of export in this quarter. 
So, the blend change will, in fact, impact the margins. But on an overall, this is the level, by and large, on 
an annual basis that we'll remain on, especially in the second half as the export delivery picks up pace; it 
will be slightly higher margins compared to obviously the turnkey segment. 
 
Gaurav Giridhar 
Okay. Thank you so much. I'll come back in queue. 
 
Rahul Mithal 
Thanks.

Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you have a question, please press * and 1 on your telephone keypad. 
We have the next question from the line of Mr. Vishal Periwal from PL Capital. Please go ahead. 
 
Vishal Periwal 
Yes. Thanks for the opportunity. Sir, a brief has been provided in the presentation that the delivery for the 
Bangladesh coaches has begun. So, I think it is mentioned one rake is already delivered. In terms of more 
numbers, can you provide, like, in this quarter, how many are expected? And then at Q4, I mean, what

Rahul Mithal 
So, yes, Vishal, morning. As I mentioned, this first rake -- being the first rake, it required a lot of final 
checks, inspection by third party, etc. So, while we were targeting it at Q2, it slid by about 10-12 days. And 
in fact, that has had an impact both on the top line and the commensurate bottom line of Q2. But once 
the first rake has gone and it is now being put into service there very shortly in Bangladesh. So the learning 
experience for both us and Bangladesh Railway will expedite the production for the subsequent rakes. 
I foresee that regular basis, while in the second quarter -- I mean, the Q3, the second rake would near 
completion. But again, revenue booking, as you know, in export happens in final dispatch. So, I would -- 
while the efforts are on, but I think the deliveries of these subsequent rakes would happen Q4 onwards. 
And whether it is about two rakes or three rakes, we will try and fine tune. And by the end of this quarter, 
we'll get a better picture, but definitely, at least about two rakes minimum in Q3/ Q4.

Okay. So, we have total 10 rakes, one is delivered, another two in the remaining part of financial year and 
then seven will go to FY28. Is that fair to understand?

Yes, very much so. In fact, the balance seven rakes will pick up pace very soon after the second rake 
onwards because, when the design and the manufacturing and the acceptance will get streamlined, so, 
the seven rakes, definitely, they have to contractually also get finished in the next FY. So, the pace of 
picking up the third, fourth rake onwards will be very much faster.

Yes. Gaurav, I'm glad you raised this point. This is a very important hit that we have to account for and-

Thank you for the opportunity. Sir, could you just give a list of the export orders which are yet to be

Rahul Mithal 
Yeah, morning. So, as I think one of your -- I think Vishal had asked, the Bangladesh order, I had given the 
details about nine rakes are left, which is about 182 coaches. 18 coaches went in the first rake. And the 
major order which is pending is the FY, that is the ICVL Mozambique of five locomotives.  
So, these are the major bulk orders. And as you said, we are trying to start in a short compressed time 
because this is a recent order, but still we are stepping up, trying to start the deliveries of the Mozambique 
locomotives, at least take the first locomotive in Q4. Major export of rolling stock orders.  
Besides, there are orders for the development that we did for conversion of the in-service diesel

Park Medi World Limited  | Q2 & H1 FY’27 Investor Presentation
Dr. Ankit Gupta
Managing Director
“H1 FY’27 has been a period of record growth and significant investment for Park Medi World. We treated more than half
a million patients and delivered our highest-ever half-yearly Revenue of INR 9,867 mn, up 22% YoY, with Q2 Revenue rising
25% to a record INR 5,110 mn. At the same time, we added 680 beds in just six months through Rudrapur and Panchkula,
taking our capacity to 4,290 beds.
As expected, onboarding this new capacity has had a near-term bearing on occupancy and profitability, as new
facilities take time to ramp up. With the commissioning of Febris (Delhi), the Palam Vihar expansion (Gurugram), Mehar
Hospital (Zirakpur) and the Kanpur facility, we expect total additions of 1,430 beds in FY’27 — c.40% over our FY’26 closing
capacity and the largest addition in our history. Our priorities now are the seamless integration of these assets, improving
utilisation and margins. With cash of INR 3,713 mn against term debt of INR 1,779 mn, we have the balance sheet strength
to fund this growth while remaining committed to affordable, high-quality healthcare and long-term value for all our
stakeholders."

Gurugram, November 13th, 2026: Park Medi World Limited, North India’s 2nd largest hospital chain (“the Company”) 
(NSE: PARKHOSPS, BSE: 544645) today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended

Notes to the unaudited Consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 
30, 2026 
1. The unaudited Consolidated financial results of Park Medi World Limited (‘the Company’) for 
the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, were reviewed by the Audit committee 
on November 13, 2026, and approved by the Board of Directors at its meeting held on 
November 13, 2026, in terms of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 as amended ("Listing Regulations"), and have been 
subjected to limited review by the statutory auditors of the Company who have issued an 
unmodified opinion on the same. 
2. The aforesaid unaudited Consolidated financial results have been prepared in accordance with 
the recognition and measurement principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standards (Ind 
AS) - 34 “Interim Financial Reporting” notified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 
(“the Act”) read with the Companies (Indian Accounting Standard Rules), 2015 (as amended 
from time to time) and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in terms of 
Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. 
3. During the quarter: 
i. The Company has successfully acquired 80% shareholding of V3 Healthcare Private Limited 
on July 31, 2026 which operates a multi-super speciality Hospital in the name of “The 
Medicity Hospital’, Rudrapur, Uttarakhand, having capacity of 330 beds. Remaining 20% 
will be acquired by April 30, 2030. Overall cost of acquisition is approx. Rs. 1,628.40 millions 
with proximate valuation from a merchant banker/chartered accountant. Consequent to 
this acquisition, V3 Healthcare Private Limited has become a subsidiary of the Company. 
Further, the Hospital has been launched on August 2, 2026 under current management. 
ii. The Company has incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary in the name of Park Medicity 
Prayagraj Limited on September 08, 2026. This entity is for the development and operation 
of a 550 bed multi super-speciality hospital in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. This hospital has 
been awarded to the Company under the Public-Private Relationship (PPP) model by the 
Prayagraj Municipal Corporation, Uttar Pradesh. 
iii. Aggarwal Hospital and Research Services Private Limited a wholly owned subsidiary 
of the Company has entered into operation and management agreement with Axis 
Educational Society (AES) for operating and managing a 300 bed multi-super 
speciality hospital, namely Axis Hospital and Research Centre located in Kanpur, 
Uttar Pradesh, for a term of 28 years w.e.f April 01, 2027. 
iv. The Company in its Board Meeting held on August 03, 2026 has approved the proposal to 
acquire 100% stake in Mehar Mediserve LLP by December 03, 2026. The LLP owns Mehar 
Hospital located at Zirakpur, Punjab. Mehar Hospital is a well-established multi super 
speciality institution with a capacity of 150+ beds. 
4. Post closure of the reporting period, some of the premises inter-alia related to the Company, 
some of its subsidiaries and officials of the Company, were subject to search or survey by the 

Income Tax Department from October 12, 2026 to October 17, 2026. There has been no 
impact on our operations, commitments and expansion plans. 
5. The Group's business activity primarily falls within a single reportable business segment 
namely "Healthcare Service" and operates primarily in India and accordingly does not have 
any additional disclosure to be made under Ind AS 108- "Segment Reporting". The Group does 
not distinguish revenues, costs and expenses between segments in its internal reporting, and 
report costs and expenses by nature as a whole. The Board of Directors (Chief Operating 
Decision Maker ("CODM") reviews the Consolidated Financial information when making 
decisions about allocating resources and assessing performance of the Group as a whole and 
hence, the Group has only one reportable segment. The Group operates and manages its 
business as a single segment mainly through the sale of healthcare services. The Group 
operates in one geographic segment namely "within India" and hence no separate information 
for geographic segment wise disclosure is required.

Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Supriya Lifescience Limited Q2 FY27 
Earnings Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will 
be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on 
your touchtone phone. Please note that this call is being recorded. I now hand over the 
conference to Ms. Sneha Salian from EY Investor Relations. Thank you, and over to you, 
ma'am. 
Sneha Salian: 
Thank you, Arshi. A warm welcome to all the participants to the Supriya Lifescience Limited 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. The investor presentation and the financial results are 
available on the company's website and on the stock exchanges. Please note anything said on 
this call, which reflects our outlook for the future, or which can be construed as a forward-
looking statement must be viewed in conjunction with the risks that the company faces.  
This conference call is being recorded and the transcript along with the audio of the same will 
be made available on the website of the company as well as on the exchanges. Please also note 
that the audio of the conference call is copyright material of Supriya Lifescience Limited and it 
cannot be copied, rebroadcasted or attributed in press or media without specific and written 
consent of the company.  
To give you a brief business update and to take you through the results, from the management 
team, we have Dr. Saloni Wagh, Managing Director; Ms. Shivani Wagh, Joint Managing 
Director; and Mr. Krishna Raghunathan, Chief Financial Officer. I would now request Ms. 
Shivani Wagh to provide you with a brief update on the quarter. Over to you, ma'am. 
Shivani Wagh: 
Good evening, everyone. I am Shivani Wagh, Joint Managing Director of Supriya Lifescience 
Limited. It is a pleasure to welcome you all to our Q2 FY '27 earnings call. Before we begin, I 
would like to take this opportunity to wish you and your families a very happy and prosperous 
festive season. With that, let me take you through our performance for the quarter. 
 
I hope you have had the opportunity to review our results and investor presentation. Revenue 
for the quarter stood at INR206 crores, registering growth of 3.2% year-on-year. Our sales 
performance during the quarter was impacted by regulatory changes in the LATAM market, 
which affected demand for certain products. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR45 crores, a 
decline of 37.5%, with an EBITDA margin of 22%.  
Let me briefly touch upon the key factors that impacted our margins during the quarter. Firstly, 
the regulatory changes in LATAM market affected demand for some of our higher-margin 
products. This resulted in a shift in our product and geographic mix with a higher share of 
sales coming from semi-regulated markets during the quarter.  
Secondly, we incurred higher operating expenses at our Ambernath facility, which is currently 
in the ramp-up phase. As commercial production and sales from the facility scale up in the 
coming quarters, we expect to see better absorption of these costs and an improvement in 
operating leverage.  
SUPRIYA LIFESCIENCE LTD. 

 
 
Supriya Lifescience Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 16 
 
Thirdly, due to the ongoing war and geopolitical tensions, raw material and solvent prices 
remained high, which has also impacted on our margins during the quarter. While these factors 
weighed on margins, we remain focused on improving our product mix, scaling up new 
launches and driving better operating leverage from our investments.  
Moving to our geographical performance. Exports continued to be a key contributor to the 
business, accounting for 80% of revenue in Q2 FY '27. Within exports, Europe contributed 
43%; Asia, 36%; and LATAM, 12%.  
Before I move on, I would like to take a moment to welcome Mr. Mangesh Vaze, who has 
joined us as our Chief Operating Officer. With over 30 years of experience in API 
manufacturing and operations, he will lead operations across our API and formulation 
businesses. We are pleased to have Mr. Mangesh Vaze on board.  
Coming back to business, we continue to make steady progress on our backward integration 
strategy. Products that are fully backward integrated now account for approximately 74% of 
total revenue, giving us greater control over our supply chain and cost structure.  
Coming to new product launches, as guided in our Q1 FY '27 earnings call, we launched 2 new 
anesthetic liquid inhalation products from our Ambernath facility during Q2 FY '27. These 
products are currently in early stages of commercialization, and we expect their contribution to 
increase progressively over the coming quarters. In addition, we have 2 ADHD products in the 
pipeline, which will further expand our portfolio and contribute to growth as they are 
commercialized.  
We are also seeing encouraging traction in the products launched during FY '26, which gives 
us confidence in the strength of our product pipeline and the opportunities ahead. Looking 
ahead, we remain focused on achieving our INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by FY '27. Our 
growth outlook continues to be supported by a healthy product pipeline and demand across key 
therapeutic segments, including anesthetics, antidiabetics, anti-anxiety, vitamins and ADHD.  
At the same time, considering our current product and geographic mix, the ramp-up phase of 
the Ambernath facility and the prevailing raw material and solvent prices, we are revising our 
EBITDA margin guidance downwards to 23% - 25%. We expect the margin profile to improve 
progressively as commercial sales from Ambernath scale up, the product mix improves and 
raw material and solvent costs normalize.  
As we have highlighted previously, growth may remain nonlinear across quarters as new 
products scale up, and market conditions evolve. However, our underlying growth drivers 
remain firmly in place, and we remain confident in the medium-term prospects of the business.  
With that, I now invite our CFO, Mr. Krishna Raghunathan to take you through the detailed 
financial performance for Q2 FY '27. 
Krishna Raghunathan: 
Thank you, Shivani. Good evening, everyone. Let me take you all through the operational 
highlights of the quarter, following which we will open the floor for questions and answers. 
For Q2 FY '27, the company reported revenue from operations of INR206 crores as against

quarters. As far as the regulatory change goes, a lot of our high-margin controlled products in 
LATAM have recently been categorized as controlled substances. 
 
So earlier, they were getting freely imported across several markets like Colombia, Peru, 
Uruguay. So, these markets now have made these products controlled because of which a lot of 
our customers now have to apply for import authorizations for these products. And because 
this is a regulatory change, which has recently happened, most of the customers are now in the 
process of getting their import authorization. So once the import authorizations are received by 
the customers, business will continue as normal. But typically, this process does take a couple

So, what is the proportion of our total business that gets affected in the intermediate term? And

And now for any shipment, they will have to get the import authorization.  
And this has not happened in only one country. It happened in 3, 4 countries together where

are taking a bit of a time. So that's one of the main reasons why I would say the product mix 
has sort of changed. So instead of these high-margin products moving in those markets, that 
volume got impacted.  
And at the same time, the new launch products that we have done in the last couple of quarters, 
they are seeing good traction, but that is mainly happening in semi-regulated markets where 
the average selling prices for the products are not as high as the regulated markets. So that is 
the reason the product mix as well as the market mix has changed, which has impacted the 
margins mainly.

and the solvent prices. So, at a very broad level, this would be the main percentage

better controls in the raw materials, solvents and trying to push the sale more in regulated 
markets of the other products. So, we are trying to improve that as much as possible. 
 
But yes, once this year is completed, Ambernath comes into operation, we are scheduled for an 
EU audit in the month of November for Ambernath, in fact, starting next week. So once that 
approval is in place and the products start moving from that site as well and start contributing, 
the sales to LATAM are regularized, new products scale up in regulated markets for the next 
year, we expect the margin profile to sort of normalize.

products. This resulted in a shift in our product and geographic mix with a higher share of 
sales coming from semi-regulated markets during the quarter.

in the ramp-up phase. As commercial production and sales from the facility scale up in the 
coming quarters, we expect to see better absorption of these costs and an improvement in 
operating leverage.

launches and driving better operating leverage from our investments.

total revenue, giving us greater control over our supply chain and cost structure.

any working capital limits except for letter of credit and bank guarantees. With that, we can 
open the floor for questions and answers. Thank you.

So just wanted to understand a bit better on this issue on the regulatory side in LATAM. Can

hence margins and the overall business? 
Dr. Saloni Wagh: 
So no, let me correct you. The margin profile dip is not on a permanent basis. This is more of a 
transient midterm kind of a situation, which we are expecting to correct over the next couple of 
quarters. As far as the regulatory change goes, a lot of our high-margin controlled products in 
LATAM have recently been categorized as controlled substances. 
 
So earlier, they were getting freely imported across several markets like Colombia, Peru, 
Uruguay. So, these markets now have made these products controlled because of which a lot of 
our customers now have to apply for import authorizations for these products. And because 
this is a regulatory change, which has recently happened, most of the customers are now in the 
process of getting their import authorization. So once the import authorizations are received by 
the customers, business will continue as normal. But typically, this process does take a couple 
of months. And that is why we believe it's just a short to midterm kind of an impact and not a 
long-term impact on margins. 
Aashish: 
So, what is the proportion of our total business that gets affected in the intermediate term? And 
so, is this effective immediately, is it what the regulation there is? I mean people are not aware 
of the fact that there was no advance notice on this. Is it that way?

Supriya Lifescience Limited 
 
 
November 06, 2026

Dr. Saloni Wagh:

time given for the customers to sort of, import and keep some stock. So, it was made effective.

And this has not happened in only one country. It happened in 3, 4 countries together where 
they changed the regulations of classifying this product as controlled because of which they 
are taking a bit of a time. So that's one of the main reasons why I would say the product mix 
has sort of changed. So instead of these high-margin products moving in those markets, that 
volume got impacted.  
And at the same time, the new launch products that we have done in the last couple of quarters,

the average selling prices for the products are not as high as the regulated markets. So that is

Management Commentary
"The Company reported sequential growth in Q2 FY27, with Revenue from Operations increasing by 6.9% quarter-on-quarter to ₹5,063 million, supported by steady 
execution of its solar pump order book despite a competitive pricing environment. Operating EBITDA stood at ₹574 million, with a margin of 11.3%, while PAT* stood at 
₹396 million, translating into a margin of 7.7%.
Operating EBITDA margin reduced by 437 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily due to higher raw material costs and increased operating expenses. Higher raw 
material costs accounted for approximately 210 basis points of the decline, driven by an increase in aluminium frame, glass and copper prices, as well as higher zinc and 
steel costs at the Company’s subsidiary, Walso Solar Solutions Private Limited, particularly in relation to orders secured at earlier input cost levels. The remaining 227 basis 
points were attributable to higher employee costs associated with strengthening the Company's workforce to support the scale-up of its Solar EPC business, increased 
project related operating expenses, and higher debtors provisions resulting from the applicable accounting standard. Consequently, PAT* margin declined by 343 basis 
points quarter-on-quarter to 7.7%, largely reflecting the decline in operating profitability.
The Company's solar pump order book currently stands at 9,487 pumps, complemented by a near-term pipeline of approximately 10,000 pumps across direct PM-KUSUM, 
Magel Tyala, indirect PM-KUSUM and export opportunities, providing visibility on future execution.
Against the backdrop of delays in the rollout of PM-KUSUM 2.0, the Company continues to strategically diversify its revenue streams beyond its core government-led solar 
irrigation business. It is actively expanding its presence across Rooftop Solar, Utility-Scale Solar and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Solar EPC segments. The combined order 
book across these segments currently stands at approximately 143 MW, and a robust pipeline of 168 MW. This diversification is expected to broaden the Company's 
addressable market, strengthen its revenue base and create additional avenues for long-term growth.
Further strengthening its backward integration capabilities, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Oswal Solar Energy Private Limited, has announced plans 
to establish a 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility, subject to shareholders' approval. This strategic initiative is aimed at securing a reliable supply of Domestic 
Content Requirement (DCR)-compliant solar cells, enhancing supply chain integration and improving cost competitiveness over the medium to long term. Solar cell 
manufacturing will not only improve its supply chain and market competitiveness, but will also improve the margin profile of the company.
Looking ahead, the Company remains focused on disciplined execution of its order book, restoring operating margins through cost optimisation and operational 
efficiencies, and building a more diversified and integrated business platform to drive sustainable growth and long-term value creation for all stakeholders."
-Vivek Gupta 
Chairman and Managing Director, Oswal Pumps Limited

Management Commentary
"The Company reported sequential growth in Q2 FY27, with Revenue from Operations increasing by 6.9% quarter-on-quarter to ₹5,063 million, supported by steady 
execution of its solar pump order book despite a competitive pricing environment. Operating EBITDA stood at ₹574 million, with a margin of 11.3%, while PAT* stood at 
₹396 million, translating into a margin of 7.7%.
Operating EBITDA margin reduced by 437 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily due to higher raw material costs and increased operating expenses. Higher raw 
material costs accounted for approximately 210 basis points of the decline, driven by an increase in aluminium frame, glass and copper prices, as well as higher zinc and 
steel costs at the Company’s subsidiary, Walso Solar Solutions Private Limited, particularly in relation to orders secured at earlier input cost levels. The remaining 227 basis 
points were attributable to higher employee costs associated with strengthening the Company's workforce to support the scale-up of its Solar EPC business, increased 
project related operating expenses, and higher debtors provisions resulting from the applicable accounting standard. Consequently, PAT* margin declined by 343 basis 
points quarter-on-quarter to 7.7%, largely reflecting the decline in operating profitability.
The Company's solar pump order book currently stands at 9,487 pumps, complemented by a near-term pipeline of approximately 10,000 pumps across direct PM-KUSUM, 
Magel Tyala, indirect PM-KUSUM and export opportunities, providing visibility on future execution.
Against the backdrop of delays in the rollout of PM-KUSUM 2.0, the Company continues to strategically diversify its revenue streams beyond its core government-led solar 
irrigation business. It is actively expanding its presence across Rooftop Solar, Utility-Scale Solar and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Solar EPC segments. The combined order 
book across these segments currently stands at approximately 143 MW, and a robust pipeline of 168 MW. This diversification is expected to broaden the Company's 
addressable market, strengthen its revenue base and create additional avenues for long-term growth.
Further strengthening its backward integration capabilities, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Oswal Solar Energy Private Limited, has announced plans 
to establish a 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility, subject to shareholders' approval. This strategic initiative is aimed at securing a reliable supply of Domestic 
Content Requirement (DCR)-compliant solar cells, enhancing supply chain integration and improving cost competitiveness over the medium to long term. Solar cell 
manufacturing will not only improve its supply chain and market competitiveness, but will also improve the margin profile of the company.
Looking ahead, the Company remains focused on disciplined execution of its order book, restoring operating margins through cost optimisation and operational 
efficiencies, and building a more diversified and integrated business platform to drive sustainable growth and long-term value creation for all stakeholders."
-Vivek Gupta

Total Income stood at ₹5,118 million in Q2 FY27, up 6.2% QoQ 
 
Karnal, Haryana, 13th November 2026: Oswal Pumps Limited, one of the most trusted name in the Solar Pumps 
manufacturing, announced its Q2 FY27 results yesterday. The Board of Directors of Oswal Pumps Limited at its 
meeting held on 12th November 2026 took on record the unaudited Financial Results for the second quarter of 
Financial Year 2026-27.

Commenting on the results, Mr. Vivek Gupta, Chairman and Managing Director, Oswal Pumps Limited, said: 
 
“The Company reported sequential growth in Q2 FY27, with Total Income increasing by 6.2% quarter-on-quarter to ₹5,118 
million. Revenue from Operations increased by 6.9% quarter-on-quarter to ₹5,063 million, supported by steady execution of its 
solar pump order book despite a competitive pricing environment. EBITDA stood at ₹628 million, with a margin of 12.3%. 
Operating EBITDA stood at ₹574 million, with a margin of 11.3%, while PAT stood at ₹396 million, translating into a margin of 
7.7%. 
Operating EBITDA margin reduced by 437 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily due to higher raw material costs and 
increased operating expenses. Higher raw material costs accounted for approximately 210 basis points of the decline, driven by 
an increase in aluminium frame, glass and copper prices, as well as higher zinc and steel costs at the Company’s subsidiary, 
Walso Solar Solutions Private Limited, particularly in relation to orders secured at earlier input cost levels. The remaining 227 
basis points were attributable to higher employee costs associated with strengthening the Company's workforce to support the 
scale-up of its Solar EPC business, increased project related operating expenses, and higher debtors provisions resulting from the 
applicable accounting standard. Consequently, PAT margin declined by 343 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 7.7%, largely 
reflecting the decline in operating profitability. 
The Company's pump order book currently stands at 9,487 pumps, complemented by a near-term pipeline of approximately 
10,000 pumps across direct PM-KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM-KUSUM and export opportunities, providing visibility on future 
execution. 
Against the backdrop of delays in the rollout of PM-KUSUM 2.0, the Company continues to strategically diversify its revenue 
streams beyond its core government-led solar irrigation business. It is actively expanding its presence across Rooftop Solar, 
Utility-Scale Solar and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Solar EPC segments. The combined order book across these segments 
currently stands at approximately 143 MW, and a robust pipeline of 168 MW. This diversification is expected to broaden the 
Company's addressable market, strengthen its revenue base and create additional avenues for long-term growth. 

 
Page | 2 
 
Further strengthening its backward integration capabilities, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Oswal Solar 
Energy Private Limited, has announced plans to establish a 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility at Karnal, Haryana. 
The total project cost is estimated at approximately ₹4,558.5 million, of which ₹2,960.0 million is proposed to be funded through 
debt and ₹1598.5 million through the reallocation of unutilised IPO proceeds originally earmarked for the aluminium frame 
manufacturing facility, the remaining 300 MW EVA encapsulant capacity and the remaining 500 MW solar module capacity, 
subject to shareholders’ approval. 
This strategic initiative is expected to meet approximately 75% of the subsidiary's solar cell requirements, ensuring a reliable 
supply of Domestic Content Requirement (DCR)-compliant cells while reducing dependence on external suppliers. By extending 
backward integration into solar cell manufacturing, the Company aims to enhance supply chain efficiencies, strengthen cost 
competitiveness and improve its overall margin profile over the medium to long term.  
Looking ahead, the Company remains focused on disciplined execution of its order book, restoring operating margins through 
cost optimisation and operational efficiencies, and building a more diversified and integrated business platform to drive 
sustainable growth and long-term value creation for all stakeholders.” 
 
Milestones Achieved in Q2 FY27 
 
• 
Total income of ₹ 5,118 Mn in Q2 FY27 
 
• 
EBITDA of ₹ 628 Mn in Q2 FY27. EBITDA Margin was at 12.3%   
 
• 
PAT* of ₹ 396 Mn in Q2 FY27. PAT Margin was at 7.7% 
 
• 
Diluted EPS stood at ₹ 3.34 in Q2 FY27  
 
“Milestones Achieved in H1 FY27” 
 
• 
Total income of ₹ 9,934 Mn in H1 FY27 
 
• 
EBITDA of ₹ 1,453 Mn in H1 FY27. EBITDA Margin was at 14.6%   
 
• 
PAT* of ₹ 935 Mn in H1 FY27. PAT Margin was at 9.4% 
 
• 
Diluted EPS stood at ₹ 8.20 in H1 FY27  
 
*Profit for the period attributable to the owners of the parent 
 
About Oswal Pumps Limited 
 
Oswal Pumps is one of India’s fastest-growing, vertically integrated solar pump manufacturer. With a legacy of over two decades 
in pump engineering and manufacturing, the company is a fully integrated provider of turnkey solar pumping systems. It has 
established a strong presence across solar-powered and grid-connected submersible and monoblock pumps, electric motors, and 
solar modules—all marketed under the trusted ‘Oswal’ brand. 
 
The Company is accredited with ISO 9001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, and ISO 14001:2015 certifications and is listed under the Ministry 
of New and Renewable Energy’s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM). 
 
With a strong pan-India distribution network, growing international footprint across countries, and a focused design and 
engineering team, Oswal Pumps continues to cater to the diverse requirements of end-users in the agricultural, residential and 
industrial sectors.
